title: MAS to boost Singapore equities market with education, guardrails and a risk‑taking framework
body: MAS deputy chairman Chee Hong Tat announced increased resources for public and investor education, new guardrails and a more risk‑taking approach to revive Singapore’s equities market, while emphasizing transparency, shareholder engagement and stronger enforcement. He also responded to Workers’ Party proposals, noting that some value‑creation disclosures may become mandatory but stressing that not all measures should be prescribed.

title: SGX posts strongest half‑year results since 2000, driven by higher trading volumes and IPO activity
body: SGX reported a half‑year net profit of $342.7 million (up 0.8%) and revenue of $736.2 million (up 7.9%), with daily average securities trading value rising 20% to $1.51 billion—the highest in five years, and an interim dividend of 21.75 cents per share, up 20.8% year‑on‑year. The exchange attributed the performance to stronger multi‑asset trading, a robust IPO pipeline of more than 30 companies and the Equity Market Development Programme supported by the Monetary Authority of Singapore.

title: Yangzijiang Shipbuilding fell about 5.6% after a drop in Maersk earnings and job‑cut plans, pulling Singapore's Straits Times Index down 0.7%
body: Yangzijiang Shipbuilding’s shares slid 5.3% to 5.6% in early trading, erasing over S$700 million in market value, after Maersk reported lower earnings and announced plans to cut 1,000 jobs, with Maersk shares down 3.7% in Copenhagen. The broader market saw the STI down 0.7% and declines in DBS (‑0.7%), OCBC (‑0.9%) and Singtel (‑0.8%), while regional indices and US tech stocks also fell.

title: SGX posts modest profit rise, raises interim dividend and highlights strong IPO pipeline
body: SGX reported H1 FY2026 adjusted net profit of S$357.1 million (up 11.6%) with revenue of S$736.2 million and declared an interim dividend of S$0.11 per share payable on Feb 24. CEO Loh Boon Chye said trading broadened across sectors, institutional investors bought S$415 million of small‑ and mid‑cap stocks, the exchange raised nearly S$3 billion from IPOs and is preparing a Global Listing Board to attract more high‑growth companies.

title: Keppel shares jump as it proposes 13‑cent dividend while M1 stake sale to Simba Telecom faces regulatory delay
body: Keppel's shares rose over 6% after announcing a 13‑cent special dividend, but the expected $1.43 billion sale of its 83.9% stake in M1 to Simba Telecom is delayed pending regulatory approval, with cash proceeds of about $1 billion slated for recognition in the 2026 monetisation value. The company also highlighted the need to boost occupancy at its Keppel South Central office tower before any further divestments and outlined its early‑stage AI initiatives and competitive positioning against firms such as BlackRock and Global Infrastructure Partners.

title: Asian markets slide as AI spending worries hit Singapore’s STI and crypto prices tumble
body: The Straits Times Index fell 0.8% to 4,934.41 as investors reacted to Amazon’s $200 billion AI‑related spending plan and broader tech sell‑off, dragging down blue‑chip stocks such as Yangzijiang Shipbuilding (‑6.2%), DBS (‑0.6%), OCBC (‑1%) and Singtel (‑1.3%). Bitcoin slipped to around US$63,000, a 50% drop over three months, with Maybank analysts linking the crypto decline to rising AI costs and the nomination of hawkish Fed chair candidate Kevin Warsh, while regional indices showed mixed moves.

title: Singapore Exchange posts slight profit increase amid earnings‑season rally while Singtel, Keppel and Hongkong Land announce major deals and dividend upgrades
body: Singapore Exchange SGX reported a 0.8% rise in first‑half net profit to $342.7 million and a 7.9% revenue increase, declared a 21.75 cent interim dividend and reiterated 6‑8% medium‑term revenue growth despite a modest share dip. During the same week, Singtel teamed with KKR in a $6.6 billion acquisition of ST Telemedia Global Data Centres, Keppel posted a 39% jump in FY2025 profit to $1.1 billion and proposed a 47 cent total dividend, Hongkong Land launched an $8.2 billion Singapore Central Private Real Estate Fund, and parliament debated the effectiveness of the Equity Market Development Programme.

title: Boustead Singapore moves ahead with UI Boustead REIT listing and divests industrial assets
body: Boustead Singapore received an eligibility-to-list letter from the Singapore Exchange for UI Boustead REIT and entered definitive agreements to sell its interests in 15 industrial properties, generating about $258.7 million in proceeds, of which roughly $202.8 million will be used to subscribe for a 16.9 % stake in the REIT. Metro Holdings, through its subsidiary Metrobilt Construction, will sell its 26 % stake in Boustead Industrial Fund to the REIT for an estimated $116 million, while Boustead shares traded at $2.15, down 1.4 % on Feb 10.

title: SGX reports 66% YoY turnover rise in January as STI gains 5.6% and new listings boost activity
body: The Singapore Exchange posted a S$34.6 billion turnover in January, up 66% year‑on‑year, with securities daily average value rising 58% to S$1.6 billion and ETF assets reaching a record S$19.1 billion. The STI climbed 5.6% month‑on‑month, while new listings such as Concord New Energy Group, The Assembly Place and Toku, and fresh ETFs including UOBAM Ping An FTSE Asean Dividend Index ETF and CSOP CSAM CSI A500 Index ETF, contributed to heightened trading across equities, derivatives and commodities.

title: Mindarie Investment's cash offer for Alpha Integrated Real Estate Investment Trust AI-Reit becomes unconditional, closing date extended to Feb 24
body: Mindarie Investment's mandatory conditional cash offer for Alpha Integrated Real Estate Investment Trust AI-Reit was declared unconditional on Feb 9 after acceptances covering about 10% of units, raising Volare and its concert parties' holdings to roughly 51.2% of the REIT’s issued units. The closing date was extended to 5.30 pm on Feb 24, and UOB, the offeror’s financial adviser, said the REIT will stay listed with no material changes planned.

title: Singapore's STI breaks 5,000 points as banks rally and market reforms boost confidence
body: The Straits Times Index climbed above 5,000 on Feb 12, driven by gains in its three major banks—DBS up 0.5%, OCBC up 1.3% and UOB up 0.9%—and supported by MAS and SGX initiatives to enhance liquidity and attract listings. The rise follows a $5 billion equity market development programme, a new iEdge Singapore Next 50 Index, a dual‑listing highway with Nasdaq, and a reduced board‑lot size aimed at revitalising Singapore’s equities market.

title: OCBC downgrades Sheng Siong to hold, shares fall 4.2%
body: Sheng Siong’s shares dropped 4.2% to $2.73 after OCBC downgraded the stock to “hold,” citing a forward 12‑month P/E of 24.8 versus its 19.6 historical average. The analyst kept a defensive outlook, noted strong earnings visibility, and raised the fair‑value target to $2.89.

title: Singapore’s STI falls below 5,000 after Budget 2026 rollout as new equity‑market support measures are announced
body: The Straits Times Index slipped 1.3% to 4,949.93 points on Friday following the Budget 2026 announcements, which introduced expanded EQDP funding, a S$1.5 bn Anchor Fund tranche, a S$1 bn Startup SG Equity scheme and household cash vouchers. Analysts such as JPMorgan and Maybank remain positive, citing the fiscal surplus boost and the support for sectors including DBS, OCBC, UOB, Singtel, ST Engineering, Keppel DC Reit and other tech and consumer firms.

title: iFast reports 45.7% revenue growth and record AUA in Q4 2025, proposes higher dividend and announces stake acquisition
body: iFast posted Q4 2025 revenue of S$151.7 million, up 45.7% year‑on‑year, net profit of S$32.9 million and a final dividend of S$0,025 per share, while its banking arm iFast Global Bank achieved its first full‑year profit; the group’s assets under administration reached a record S$31.98 billion and it conditionally agreed to acquire a 30% stake in Financial Alliance Corporation to link its wealth platform with advisory services.

title: Lum Chang Creations receives SGX approval to transfer from Catalist to the mainboard after reporting a 104% profit increase
body: Lum Chang Creations was granted in‑principal approval by the Singapore Exchange to move to the mainboard, subject to shareholder approval, and reported first‑half net profit of S$11 million, up 104% year‑on‑year. Its parent, Lum Chang Holdings, holds a 71.1% stake and the company was added to the MSCI Global Micro Cap Indexes – Singapore Index effective Feb 27.

title: Singapore's STI retreats after Budget 2026 despite new equity and startup support measures
body: Following the Budget 2026 announcement, the Straits Times Index slipped 1.6% to 4,936.51 points before closing the day at 4,937.78, with bank stocks DBS, OCBC and UOB falling 1.2%‑3.1% and Singtel down 1.8%, while the government pledged an extra S$1.5 billion for the Anchor Fund, S$1 billion for the Startup SG Equity Scheme and a revised surplus of S$15.1 billion; analysts such as JPMorgan and Maybank remain bullish, citing a sustained AI boom, a fiscal buffer and sectoral benefits for firms including DBS, UOB, SGX, UOL, Keppel DC Reit, ST Engineering, Addvalue Tech, AEM, Frencken, UMS and CapitaLand Integrated Commercial Trust.

title: Singapore adds $1.5 bn to the Financial Sector Development Fund to expand the Equity Market Development Programme
body: The 2026 Budget announced a further S$1.5 bn top‑up to the Financial Sector Development Fund, boosting the $5 bn Equity Market Development Programme (EQDP) that has already attracted about $13 bn of market funding and lifted SGX main‑board market capitalisation by S$173 bn since February 2025. Industry participants including UBS, Deloitte, DBS, Maybank Securities, CMC Invest, EY and Bank of Singapore said the injection reinforces market confidence, supports more high‑quality fund managers and is part of a broader ecosystem push involving new MAS‑MTI workgroups and initiatives such as the Value Unlock programme.

title: STI climbs to 5,000 points as budget boosts equity reforms and sparks calls for unit‑share and fractional trading
body: The Straits Times Index crossed the 5,000‑point mark on 12 February alongside Finance Minister Lawrence Wong’s Budget 2026, validating JPMorgan’s earlier bull target and prompting a S$1.5 billion top‑up to the Financial Sector Development Fund for the Equity Market Development Programme that involves JPMorgan, Avanda and Fullerton; the article also urges the market to abandon odd‑lot trading in favour of unit shares and fractional investing, citing DBS and Malaysia’s recent fractional‑share launch as examples.

title: SGX faces criticism over removal of watch list and handling of zombie firms amid regional tightening
body: Singapore Exchange’s decision to drop its financial watch list has drawn criticism from market observers who warn that the lack of a mechanism to cull loss‑making “zombie” firms could harm market quality, especially on the Catalist board where 86% of listings trade below IPO price. By contrast, Korea and Japan are tightening delisting rules, and experts such as James Leong of Grasshopper Asia, Lee Ooi Keong of Clover Point Consultants and Jimmy Seet of PwC Singapore argue that stronger disclosure and governance standards are needed to balance competitiveness with investor protection.

title: SGX RegCo urges forward‑looking disclosures while outlining legal risks and governance safeguards for listed companies
body: The Singapore Exchange’s regulator released guidance encouraging forward‑guidance disclosures, stressing that statements must be based on reasonable assumptions, qualified, and overseen by the board to avoid liability under the Securities and Futures Act and Companies Act. It also noted potential adoption of U.S. safe‑harbour provisions for forward‑looking statements on the upcoming SGX‑Nasdaq Global Listing Board.

title: Singapore data‑centre REITs post strong 2025 revenue growth but share prices remain flat amid AI‑driven demand and interest‑rate concerns
body: Keppel DC REIT, Digital Core REIT and NTT DC REIT all reported double‑digit revenue gains in 2025 on AI‑related demand—Keppel DC REIT’s revenue rose 42.2% to $441.4 million with DPU up 9.8% to 10.4 cents, Digital Core REIT’s revenue jumped 72.2% to $176.2 million while its DPU held at 3.6 US cents, and NTT DC REIT saw a modest 1.7% revenue increase—but the three pure‑play REITs traded largely flat, with performance tied to future DPU growth and potential interest‑rate moves.

title: Singapore market rallies post‑Chinese New Year as DBS, OCBC and other stocks lead gains
body: The Straits Times Index rose from about 4,938 before the holiday to open above 4,986 and close over 5,017 on Feb 20, driven by gains in DBS Bank (near $58), OCBC Bank (up to $21.72), Singtel, Yangzijiang Shipbuilding, Genting Singapore and mid‑cap names such as Food Empire and Civmec. At the same time Vicom posted a 77.6% profit jump and SIA Engineering reported a 9.7% profit rise ahead of earnings season, while gold surged above $5,100 per ounce after President Trump’s Iran warning and US Q4 GDP growth missed expectations, with several Singapore firms slated to report later in the week.

title: Singapore bourse sees STI dip as UOB profit falls, while iEdge Singapore Next 50 Index climbs
body: The Straits Times Index fell 0.4% to 5,020.79 as all three local banks—UOB, DBS and OCBC—traded lower, with UOB dropping 4.1% after reporting a 7% decline in Q4 profit to S$1.41 billion and cutting its 2026 fee‑income growth outlook. Meanwhile, the iEdge Singapore Next 50 Index rose 0.4% to 1,526.98 and Yangzijiang Shipbuilding led gains on the blue‑chip index, up 2.6%.

title: UI Boustead REIT targets up to $1.02 billion in Singapore IPO, the largest since Netlink NBN Trust in 2017
body: UI Boustead REIT is offering 1.1 billion units at 88 cents each, aiming to raise up to $1.02 billion (including a $48.1 million overallotment) and would be valued at about $1.2 billion, with cornerstone investors such as Amova Asset Management Asia, JPMorgan Asset Management Singapore, Amundi’s Singapore and Malaysia entities and Jumbo Group of Restaurants committing $377.7 million. The REIT, which holds 23 logistics and industrial assets in Singapore and Japan, projects a 7.8% distribution yield for the year ending March 31 2027 and is set to list on the Singapore Exchange on March 12.

title: Singapore's STI drops 0.9% as banks slide and Seatrium posts profit surge
body: The Straits Times Index fell 0.9% to 4,964.38, with all three local banks—DBS, OCBC and UOB—closing in the red, while Seatrium rose 3.2% after reporting a 48.3% jump in H2 net profit to $179.3 million and a full‑year profit of $323.6 million. Singapore’s factory output surged 16.6% YoY in January, but regional markets were mixed, with Hong Kong down 1.4% and Japan up 0.3%.

title: AEM Holdings shares jump as AI testing demand drives profit surge and strong 2026 outlook
body: AEM Holdings reported a 47.8% rise in net profit to $17.1 million and a 5% increase in 2025 revenue to $399.3 million, while guiding 2026 revenue between $460 million and $510 million on robust AI chip testing demand; DBS Bank analyst Amanda Tan maintained a buy call despite ongoing litigation with Advantest Test Solutions and highlighted the company’s diversification into memory testing and the supportive AI market outlook from Bank of America.

title: STI dips as Singapore banks fall and earnings surge for Yangzijiang Shipbuilding, AEM Holdings and property developers
body: The Straits Times Index slipped to 4,956 before closing near 5,000 as all three major Singapore banks – UOB, OCBC and DBS – fell after UOB reported a 23% profit decline and the other banks posted weaker earnings. At the same time, Yangzijiang Shipbuilding posted a 24.6% rise in H2 2025 net profit to 4.5 billion yuan, AEM Holdings saw shares jump 44% on a 47.8% earnings surge, and property developers City Developments CDL and UOL delivered strong 2025 results with net profit jumps of 374% and 34% respectively while raising dividend payouts.

title: MAS and Singapore Exchange launch S$30 million Value Unlock programme to boost investor engagement of listed firms
body: The Monetary Authority of Singapore and the Singapore Exchange have introduced the Value Unlock programme, allocating up to S$30 million in Equip and Elevate grants to help about 600 listed companies improve their equity stories and shareholder returns. The initiative, highlighted in a BT Correspondents podcast, emphasizes capability building and boardroom mindset change rather than regulatory compulsion, targeting mid‑cap re‑rating and long‑term value creation.

title: Manulife Investments launches Singapore Opportunities Income Strategy targeting small‑ and mid‑cap equities
body: Manulife Investments introduced the Singapore Opportunities Income Strategy, which will invest exclusively in Singapore‑listed equities across market capitalisations—particularly small‑ and mid‑cap stocks—using a bottom‑up, fundamentals‑based approach to deliver balanced dividend income and capital growth while being benchmarked to the FTSE ST All‑Share Index. The firm highlighted that Singapore equities have returned about 36% over the past year with dividend yields near 4.8%, underscoring the market’s strong performance and valuation gaps the strategy aims to exploit.

title: Singapore aims to become a regional gold hub with MAS and major banks developing trading and storage services
body: The Monetary Authority of Singapore is working with banks such as JPMorgan Chase, UBS Group, ICBC Standard Bank, DBS Group Holdings, UOB and OCBC to develop Singapore as a regional physical gold trading and storage hub amid a historic bull run in gold prices. UOB is currently the only Singaporean lender offering physical gold sales and vault services to retail customers, while OCBC is exploring a custody business for institutional and wealthy clients and the Singapore Exchange is reviewing a new gold contract.

title: Aspial Lifestyle seeks SGX mainboard listing to broaden capital access and plans share sale to meet public float requirement
body: Aspial Lifestyle, the owner of Maxi‑Cash, Lee Hwa and Goldheart brands, proposed moving from the Catalist board to the Singapore Exchange mainboard to access equity and debt markets, and its controlling shareholder Aspial Corporation will sell up to 10 million shares at S$0.34 to satisfy the 15% public‑float rule. The company reported net profit of S$80.7 million in FY2025, up from S$14.4 million in FY2021.

title: Lion Global Investors to list Singapore's first home-grown physical gold ETF on SGX
body: Lion Global Investors (LGI) will list the LionGlobal Singapore Physical Gold ETF on the Singapore Exchange on March 26, trading under the SGX tickers GLS (SGD) and GLU (USD). The initial offer runs from March 6‑20, marks LGI’s 10th ETF launch and follows its LionGlobal Singapore Physical Gold Fund, which held SG$502.2 million in assets as of Feb 27, while gold prices have recently hit a record US$5,597.23 per ounce.

title: Lion Global Investors launches Singapore Physical Gold ETF on SGX
body: Lion Global Investors, a wholly owned subsidiary of Great Eastern Holdings, will list its LionGlobal Singapore Physical Gold ETF on the Singapore Exchange on March 26, trading under the SGX tickers GLS (SGD) and GLU (USD). The initial offer runs from March 6‑20, follows a related fund that grew to $502.2 million in assets as of Feb 27, and seeks to track the LBMA Gold Price amid gold’s recent record high of $5,597.23 per ounce.

title: UI Boustead Real Estate Investment Trust launches $973.6 million IPO targeting $1.2 billion in proceeds
body: UI Boustead Real Estate Investment Trust announced an IPO of 677.2 million units at 88 cents each, aiming to raise about $1.2 billion including cornerstone commitments. The REIT, which holds 23 logistics and industrial properties in Singapore and Japan valued at $1.9 billion, forecasts a distribution yield of 7.4% for FY2026 and 7.8% for FY2027.

title: Singapore Exchange to launch Asian government bond futures as it reports record half-year performance
body: Singapore Exchange (SGX) announced it will roll out Asian government bond futures in the coming weeks, responding to growing demand for hedging tools amid volatile bond markets. The launch follows SGX’s strongest half-year since its 2000 IPO, driven by robust trading volumes across all business segments.

title: Singapore Exchange to launch Asian sovereign bond futures amid global bond market volatility
body: Singapore Exchange (SGX) announced it will offer three‑, five‑ and ten‑year futures on government bonds of India, Indonesia, Malaysia, Thailand and the Philippines, settled in US dollars and priced on a basket of up to three sovereign yields. The move comes as bond markets tumble, with investors having poured about US$16 billion into Indian bonds since its June 2024 inclusion in JPMorgan Chase’s flagship index.

title: Singapore Exchange (SGX Group) posts 45% YoY rise in February SDAV to S$2.1 billion
body: Singapore Exchange (SGX Group) said its February securities daily average value (SDAV) jumped 45% year‑on‑year to S$2.1 billion, lifting total market turnover 30% to S$38.5 billion and STI turnover 38% to S$1.42 billion. ETF turnover surged 172% YoY to S$1.1 billion and derivatives daily average volume rose 22% to 1.66 million contracts.

title: UI Boustead REIT slides 8.5% below IPO price on Singapore mainboard debut
body: UI Boustead REIT opened at 80.5 cents and closed at the same level on its March 12 mainboard debut, 8.5% below its 88‑cent IPO price, with 102.5 million units traded. The offering raised about $973.6 million, giving the REIT a market capitalisation just under $2 billion and a projected FY2027 distribution yield of 7.8%.

title: Nasdaq and Singapore Exchange launch Global Listing Board slated for mid‑2026
body: Nasdaq and the Singapore Exchange announced the Global Listing Board, a dual‑listing platform expected to go live in mid‑2026 that will let companies with at least $2 billion in market value and an Asian nexus list on both markets. The initiative aims to harmonise listing rules, cut regulatory costs and speed IPOs, positioning Nasdaq as the preferred offshore venue for high‑growth firms.

title: Maybank Securities Singapore, OCBC, iFast Corp, Phillip Securities Research, CLSA and Jefferies expand equity analyst teams as MAS and SGX boost small‑mid cap coverage
body: Several Singapore brokerages—including Maybank Securities Singapore, OCBC, iFast Corp (through its FSM Global unit), Phillip Securities Research, CLSA and Jefferies—are increasing analyst headcount to deepen coverage of small and mid‑cap stocks. The hiring surge is supported by MAS’s S$50 million 2025 enhancement of the Gems programme and reflects salary offers of S$7,000‑S$20,000 per month for analysts.

title: Singapore Exchange proposes expanded broker custody accounts to modernize post‑trade infrastructure
body: The Singapore Exchange (SGX) has announced a proposal to broaden the use of omnibus broker custody accounts, giving investors an alternative to direct Central Depository (CDP) holdings while preserving the option for direct accounts. The January press statement outlines the reform, which follows a 2023 High Court ruling on shareholder rights and aims to align Singapore’s market with international practices.

title: Singapore Companies Spend $179.6M on Share Buybacks Amid Market Volatility
body: Singapore companies including ST Engineering, Keppel, Singtel, UOB, Singapore Airlines, Singapore Exchange, Seatrium, Sats, and Genting Singapore collectively spent about S$179.6 million to repurchase roughly 27.5 million shares in early March, with each firm keeping the shares in treasury. The buybacks, conducted amid Middle East tensions that rattled markets, were aimed at boosting earnings per share and signaling excess cash, though they also raised concerns about future growth deployment.

title: Singtel leads Singapore firms in March share‑buyback spree amid market turbulence
body: Eight Singapore blue‑chip companies repurchased over S$180 million of shares in early March, with Singtel buying back about 12.9 million shares for S$63.7 million at S$4.86‑4.98 each, while ST Engineering, Keppel, UOB, Singapore Airlines, Seatrium, Sats and Genting Singapore also conducted sizable buybacks. The programmes, executed despite the fallout from the Middle‑East conflict, reduced public float and boosted earnings‑per‑share metrics for the participants.

title: Singapore courts uphold lengthy sentences for market‑manipulation of Blumont Group, Asiasons Capital and Liongold Corp
body: The Court of Appeal dismissed the appeals of John Soh Chee Wen and Quah Su‑Ling, confirming jail terms of 36 and 20 years for a scheme that wiped out about S$8 billion in market value by manipulating the shares of Blumont Group, Asiasons Capital and Liongold Corp. The judgment also highlighted Quah’s former role as chief executive of IPCO International, underscoring the breadth of the fraud involving 349 charges.

title: The Society of Remisiers (Singapore) celebrates 40 years and urges a shift to fee‑based portfolio services
body: At its 40th‑anniversary gala, The Society of Remisiers (Singapore) highlighted a move from transaction‑based trading to value‑added, fee‑based discretionary portfolio management, citing over 500 remisiers enrolled in its development programme and collaboration with MAS and SGX. The announcement comes as the Straits Times Index topped the 5,000‑point mark, underscoring the growing influence of remisiers on Singapore’s equities market liquidity.

title: SGX plans targeted secondary listings for Chinese firms with S$1 billion minimum market cap
body: SGX is exploring a new wave of Chinese secondary listings that must have a market capitalisation of at least S$1 billion and raise at least S$200 million or 10% of their market cap, whichever is lower. The focus on established companies already listed in Hong Kong, Shanghai or Shenzhen aims to address governance and disclosure weaknesses that plagued earlier S‑chip attempts.

title: SGX targets wider tech and fintech listings as daily trading value climbs 45% to $2.1 bn
body: Singapore Exchange (SGX) is expanding its sector clusters and reviewing the Catalist board to attract more technology, fintech and AI firms after average daily trading volume rose 45% year‑on‑year to $2.1 bn, the highest since 2020. The Equity Market Development Programme was increased to $6.5 bn in the 2026 Budget to support the push for new listings and deeper liquidity.

title: Stoneweg Europe Stapled Trust provides FY2025 results and FY2026 distribution guidance
body: Stoneweg Europe Stapled Trust disclosed FY2025 results and forward guidance, projecting FY2026 distribution per stapled security to be broadly in line with FY2025 and implying an 8.1% distribution yield. The REIT, with a market capitalisation of S$838.6 million and a 3.2% share‑price gain over the past year, joins other Singapore issuers such as Singtel, ST Engineering and Sats that are beginning to offer forward‑looking guidance as SGX RegCo encourages greater disclosure.

title: DBS, Genting Singapore and CapitaLand Ascendas Reit see strong retail inflows as Singapore retail buying hits S$675 million in Q1 FY2026
body: Retail investors poured S$1.87 billion into DBS, S$119.4 million into Genting Singapore and S$177.4 million into CapitaLand Ascendas Reit during the first quarter of FY2026, pushing total local‑stock net buying to S$675 million, according to SGX. CapitaLand Ascendas Reit also raised S$903.5 million through a private placement and preferential offering, despite its shares falling 9.2 % in March.

title: Singapore Exchange Group lists Lion Global Investors' physical gold ETF as MAS advances gold hub plans
body: MAS and SBMA announced new gold market initiatives, and the Lion Global Singapore Physical Gold ETF debuted on the Singapore Exchange Group on Thursday, marking the exchange's first home‑grown physical gold ETF. The listing is expected to strengthen Singapore's position as a regional gold trading hub.

title: Keppel proposes 47‑cent FY2025 dividend as it accelerates asset‑light strategy and non‑core asset sales
body: Keppel announced a total FY2025 dividend of 47 cents per share (13 cents special and 34 cents ordinary), a 38% year‑on‑year increase, funded by $1.6 billion of asset monetisation in 2025 and $2.9 billion of sales announced for the year. The group targets divesting the remaining $13.5 billion of non‑core assets by 2030, using proceeds to cut debt, invest in AI‑ready infrastructure and return capital, while its New Keppel segment posted a $1.1 billion net profit, up 39% YoY.

title: Fullerton Fund Management and 65 Equity Partners appointed to manage $1.5 bn Anchor Fund 2
body: Fullerton Fund Management and 65 Equity Partners have been appointed by the Ministry of Trade and Industry and Temasek to manage the second $1.5 billion tranche of Singapore’s Anchor Fund, aimed at supporting growth companies preparing for IPOs. Since the first tranche in 2022, SGX has seen higher IPO activity and trading volumes, with average daily value up 45% year‑on‑year to $2.1 billion in February and retail investors buying $638 million of shares in March.

title: Singapore Airlines gains 2.5%, AEM Holdings jumps 11.5% on strong results, CapitaLand Ascendas Reit unveils $1.4 bn acquisition, and Keppel slides 3% after deadline extension
body: Singapore Airlines closed at $6.66, up about 2.5% for the week, while AEM Holdings surged to $4.55, an 11.5% weekly gain after reporting a 2025 earnings beat, a 2026 revenue outlook of $460‑$510 million and a JP Morgan stake of roughly 5%. CapitaLand Ascendas Reit fell 1.5% to $2.50 as it announced a $1.4 bn asset purchase funded by a $903.5 m placement, and Keppel dropped about 3% to $11.90 following the extension of the M1 unit sale deadline to May 21.

title: The Assembly Place reports 42% revenue jump to $27 million and expands into foreign worker housing
body: The Assembly Place, which listed on SGX Catalist in January, said revenue rose 42.4% to $27 million and net profit increased 6.4% to $6.6 million for the year ended Dec 31 2025, driven by a rise in managed keys to 3,422 and occupancy of 94.4%. The co‑living operator also launched a joint‑venture dormitory for foreign workers and announced a pipeline that will add about 441 keys in Singapore and Malaysia as it pursues its 10,000‑key target by 2030.

title: Kin Productions files Catalist IPO prospectus, targeting S$56.5 million revenue and S$4 million net profit for FY2025
body: Kin Productions lodged a preliminary prospectus to list on the Singapore Exchange’s Catalist board, seeking capital to expand into event tourism and related sectors. The firm posted FY2025 net profit of about S$4 million on revenue of S$56.5 million (up from S$1.6 million profit and S$19.6 million revenue in FY2024) and said its board will recommend dividends of at least 20% of net profit for FY2025 and 30% for FY2026.

title: SGX RegCo warns issuers against repeated AGM deadline extensions
body: SGX RegCo said it will not ordinarily grant extensions for AGM and reporting deadlines, citing the required timelines of four months for AGMs, 60 days for full‑year financial statements and at least 14 days for annual reports. The regulator warned that repeated extension requests could trigger enforcement actions, including director watch‑list placements.

title: ST Engineering, Wilmar International and Singapore Exchange drive STI’s 5.6% Q1 FY2026 total return as Singtel expands buyback
body: The Straits Times Index posted a 5.6% total return in Q1 FY2026, led by technology and industrials, with ST Engineering up 28.4%, Wilmar International up 25% and Singapore Exchange up 15.8% among large‑cap stocks. Institutional inflows boosted sector participation and Singtel’s ongoing S$2 billion buy‑back programme generated a record S$274.2 million net inflow, with United Overseas Bank, OCBC and Keppel also contributing to the buy‑back spending.

title: OCBC Bank tops $100bn market cap as ST Engineering secures $600m contract and CapitaLand Investment outlines divestment plan
body: OCBC Bank surpassed $100 billion market capitalisation with shares up over 4% to S$22.38, while DBS rose 1% to S$57.55 and ST Engineering’s stock climbed to a high of S$11.20 after securing a six‑year, US$600 million marine contract. CapitaLand Investment fell 1.9% to S$2.74 as it announced accelerated China‑asset divestments and a S$439 million 2025 revaluation loss, and Yeo Hiap Seng’s shares held at 60 cents after laying off 25 staff and shifting can production to Malaysia.

title: AirTrunk targets up to US$1.5 billion IPO for Singapore REIT
body: AirTrunk has appointed Citigroup and DBS to lead a potential Singapore REIT IPO that could raise up to US$1.5 billion, with a floor of US$1 billion, slated for later in 2026. The offering would be the largest Singapore REIT listing in a decade, eclipsing NTT DC REIT’s US$773 million 2025 IPO and follows Blackstone’s 2024 acquisition of AirTrunk at a valuation of A$24 billion.

title: Singapore Exchange Securities Trading and Nasdaq Stock Market stand to benefit from Singapore’s proposed Global Listing Board legislation
body: The Singapore Parliament’s Securities and Futures (Amendment) Bill 2026, read on April 7, would create a Global Listing Board jointly run by Singapore Exchange Securities Trading and Nasdaq Stock Market, targeting IPOs with at least S$2 billion in market capitalisation and an Asian nexus. The reforms would let dual‑listing issuers use a single prospectus and give retail investors access to preliminary prospectuses.

title: Singapore Exchange sees IPO surge but calls for greater sector diversity
body: Singapore Exchange reported a rise in IPO activity, highlighted by UltraGreen.ai’s US$400 million listing – the largest non‑REIT debut in Singapore since 2017 – but its head of equities warned that sectoral diversity remains limited. The exchange and the Monetary Authority of Singapore are expanding the S$6.5 billion Equity Market Development Programme, with a S$30 million Value Unlock scheme and roughly S$4 billion already allocated to nine asset‑manager partners to broaden investor participation.

title: Singtel to Transfer 710 million Discounted Shares to Individual CDP Accounts, Enabling Direct Sale by 615,000 Singaporeans
body: Singtel will move roughly 710 million special discounted shares—about 4.3% of its stock and $3.6 bn of market value—out of the CPF Board into individual CDP accounts, allowing up to 615,000 eligible Singaporeans to sell or retain the shares directly. The transfer supports Singtel's Singtel28 growth plan, including its $6.6 bn acquisition of ST Telemedia Global Data Centres, and the shares fluctuated around $5, closing 1.4% lower at $4.96 after the bill’s introduction.

title: Singapore listed firms urged to strengthen cyber risk governance amid rising AI-driven threats
body: The Singapore Exchange requires listed issuers to treat cyber security as a board‑governed risk, mandating robust internal controls, incident‑response playbooks and timely SGXNET disclosures. Recent high‑profile breaches, such as the Qantas data leak via a Salesforce compromise and a ransomware attack on Toppan Next Tech, illustrate the heightened exposure and reinforce the need for vigilant oversight.

title: Octopus (Asia-Pacific) Holdings signs five‑year distribution deal with Grupo Osborne, receives $5 million investment
body: Octopus (Asia-Pacific) Holdings signed a five‑year deal to manage the Singapore distribution of Grupo Osborne’s premium wine and spirit portfolio. Osborne will invest $5 million in Octopus at 6.8 cents per share—a 13.33% premium to the April 9 close—while Octopus’s shares were flat at 6.1 cents on April 13.

title: Singapore Exchange (SGX) set to benefit from MAS equity boost and renewed investor interest
body: The Monetary Authority of Singapore’s expanded EQDP and upcoming SGX‑Nasdaq dual‑listing bridge are expected to lift the Singapore Exchange (SGX) and its listed constituents, with the Straits Times Index trading at a 16.8‑times P/E and a 4.5% dividend yield. Local heavyweights such as DBS, OCBC, UOB, Sembcorp, Keppel, Singtel and StarHub are highlighted as primary beneficiaries of the revived market sentiment.

title: OCBC recommends China Aviation Oil, Boustead Singapore and Info‑Tech Systems among SMID picks
body: OCBC’s equity research team recommends China Aviation Oil, Boustead Singapore and Info‑Tech Systems as three of its nine SMID picks, each with market capitalisations under S$3 billion and projected upside of 11%‑44%. The recommendations follow a sharp rise in average daily turnover for SMID stocks after the first EQDP tranche was announced in July 2025.

title: SBS Transit faces shareholder scrutiny over declining bus market share and tender losses ahead of AGM
body: Ahead of its April 23 AGM, SBS Transit disclosed that its bus market share fell to about 57% in 2024‑25 after losing the Jurong West and Tampines tenders, while it maintains a financially sustainable rail business under Singapore’s 2025 rail financing framework. The company said it is enhancing its electric‑bus capabilities, citing the Sengkang West multi‑storey depot, and is refining its bid strategy to meet Land Transport Authority criteria.

title: Oiltek’s surge to S$1 billion market cap highlights valuation gaps at Koh Brothers Eco Engineering and Koh Brothers Group
body: Oiltek’s shares have risen from its S$0.23 IPO to about S$2.40, delivering a 3,000% return, a US$350 million sustainable aviation fuel contract and a 2‑for‑1 bonus issue, which lifted its market capitalisation above S$1 billion. The rally exposes that majority owner Koh Brothers Eco Engineering (valued just over S$315 million) and ultimate parent Koh Brothers Group (market cap ~S$160 million) are trading at a discount to the value of their indirect Oiltek stakes, prompting shareholder calls for in‑specie distributions.

title: Hong Leong Asia acquires Yong Tai Loong for S$90.7 million
body: Hong Leong Asia (HLA) bought 100% of Yong Tai Loong for about S$90.7 million in cash, adding the building‑components supplier, which has net assets of roughly S$34.4 million, to its portfolio. HLA’s shares rose 1.3% to S$3.17 after the announcement.

title: SGX RegCo proposes new disclosure rules for listed companies, seeking feedback until May 22
body: SGX RegCo launched a public consultation on Apr 22 to raise transparency standards, requiring issuers to disclose remuneration KPIs, dividend policies and investor‑relations policies, with the rules slated for phased implementation from Jan 1, 2027. The consultation runs until May 22, after which the regulator will consider market feedback before finalising the requirements.

title: SGX RegCo proposes new executive remuneration disclosure rules for listed companies
body: The Singapore Exchange Regulation (SGX RegCo) announced proposals requiring listed firms to disclose the metrics used to determine executive pay, dividend policies, and investor‑relations practices, with consultation ending May 22 and phased implementation from Jan 1 2027. The rules aim to improve transparency, reduce governance risk, and boost investor confidence in Singapore’s equity market.

title: OKP Holdings defends large cash reserves and outlines capital management amid shareholder queries
body: OKP Holdings said its $588 million order book through 2031 and recent $14.88 million property sale underpin its need for strong cash reserves and a balanced capital‑management approach ahead of its April 28 AGM. The firm noted construction material costs fell to 12.1% of sales in 2025 (down from 15.8% in 2024) and will evaluate share‑buyback initiatives while focusing on cycling‑path and other transport infrastructure projects.

title: Minor International to launch $1 billion Singapore REIT to fund branded‑residence expansion
body: Minor International, Thailand’s largest hospitality group with a 126.5 billion‑baht market capitalisation, plans to seed a Singapore‑listed REIT with 14 hotels (12 in Europe, 2 in Thailand) in a US$1 billion IPO slated for before the end of 2026, targeting yields of 6‑8 %. Proceeds will fund the expansion of its emerging branded‑residences business, which already has more than 30 completed projects and 21 in the pipeline as the group shifts toward an asset‑light model.

title: CapitaLand Investment sticks to Asia-Pacific real-estate credit strategy amid private-credit market stress
body: CapitaLand Investment reaffirmed its focus on Asia-Pacific real-estate-backed private credit, highlighting $125 billion of assets under management, a $3 billion real-estate credit portfolio, the A$200 million acquisition of Wingate Group and a US$320 million raise for its CapitaLand Asia Pacific Credit Program II. IFS Capital said the broader private‑credit stress in the US and Europe is unlikely to affect its Singapore SME‑focused lending business.

title: CapitaLand Integrated Commercial Trust to acquire Paragon mall for $3.9 billion
body: CapitaLand Integrated Commercial Trust (CICT) announced a $3.9 billion acquisition of Paragon mall, funded by the $2.5 billion sale of its 100 % stake in Asia Square Tower 2 to IOI Properties, and expects higher returns. Other Singapore‑listed firms saw notable moves: Keppel sold i12 Katong for about $372 million, Frasers Centerpoint Trust is weighing a $470 million sale of White Sands, Oiltek crossed the $1 billion market‑cap threshold boosting Koh Brothers Eco Engineering and its parent Koh Brothers Group, Sheng Siong faced shareholder scrutiny over $8 million director fees, Nanofilm Technologies International posted a 24 % revenue jump to $55 million, and Kin Global debuted on the Catalist board raising $10.1 million.

title: MoneyMax Financial Services raises $44.3 million and seeks Singapore Exchange mainboard upgrade
body: MoneyMax Financial Services raised $44.3 million by issuing 53 million new shares at 83.5 cents, increasing its public float to about 16.9% to meet the requirement for a move from Catalist to the Singapore Exchange mainboard. The company posted an 87.6% year‑on‑year profit increase to $71.6 million on revenue of $541.9 million, and its shares closed up 0.6% at 88.5 cents.

title: MAS and SGX propose dual‑listing framework requiring $2 billion global market cap for SGX‑Nasdaq listings
body: The Monetary Authority of Singapore and SGX RegCo announced proposals for a Global Listing Board that would let eligible companies list simultaneously on SGX and Nasdaq using a single prospectus, subject to a $2 billion minimum global market capitalisation and a requirement to raise at least 15 % of the IPO (or $75 million) in Singapore. The rules, expected to take effect mid‑2026 pending parliamentary approval in May, also mandate a minimum retail allocation of 5 % of the Singapore tranche (or $50 million) and incorporate three US‑style safe‑harbour provisions.

title: Singapore Exchange advances SGX‑Nasdaq dual‑listing bridge, targeting S$2 billion minimum market cap
body: Singapore Exchange is moving ahead with the SGX‑Nasdaq dual‑listing bridge, with the Global Listings Board expected to launch in mid‑2026 and a minimum market capitalisation of S$2 billion. The new rules require at least 15% of the IPO value or S$75 million for the Singapore tranche, with a minimum 5% or S$50 million reserved for retail brokers.

title: Lum Chang Creations seeks shareholder approval for mainboard transfer and share placement
body: Lum Chang Creations (LCC) will hold an extraordinary general meeting on May 25 to approve a 1‑for‑1 bonus issue of up to 330 million shares, a placement of up to 7.7 million shares, and its transfer from the Catalist board to SGX’s mainboard. The urban‑revitalisation specialist reported a 104 % rise in first‑half FY2026 net profit to S$11 million and an order book of about S$132 million, including contracts worth S$31.9 million and S$31.5 million.

title: MoneyMax Financial Services completes S$44.3 million share placement ahead of SGX mainboard transfer
body: MoneyMax Financial Services placed 53 million new ordinary shares at S$0,835 each, raising S$44.3 million and representing about 5.7% of its existing share capital. The proceeds satisfy the requirements for its transfer to the Singapore Exchange mainboard on May 6, after reporting second‑half 2025 profit of S$42 million and a 3.8% rise in its share price to S$0,945.

title: Mercuria Energy Group sues Baltic Exchange over TD3C benchmark, SGX denies allegations
body: Mercuria Energy Group filed a High Court claim alleging that the Baltic Exchange’s TD3C crude tanker benchmark, produced by the SGX‑owned Baltic Exchange, failed to account for the effective closure of the Strait of Hormuz, costing Mercuria hundreds of millions of dollars. Both the Baltic Exchange and SGX have denied the allegations, saying the benchmark is calculated under robust governance and the claim has no merit.

title: City Developments Limited appoints Kwek Leng Peck as vice‑chairman
body: City Developments Limited (CDL) announced that cousin of chairman Kwek Leng Beng, Kwek Leng Peck, will become vice‑chairman effective June 1 and will also be re‑appointed as a non‑independent, non‑executive director. The filing also noted the resignation of independent director Daniel Desbaillets effective May 31. Kwek, who previously resigned in 2020 after a dispute over CDL’s $1.78 billion write‑down and $1.9 billion loss linked to the collapse of Sincere Property Group, will recuse himself from any transactions involving substantial shareholders Hong Leong Investment and Hong Realty. He also stepped down from the board of CDL’s hotel subsidiary Millennium & Copthorne Hotels.

title: Singapore Parliament passes amendment to facilitate dual listings on SGX and Nasdaq by mid‑2026
body: The Securities and Futures (Amendment) Bill, approved on May 7, creates a Global Listing Board that will allow companies to list simultaneously on the Singapore Exchange (SGX) and Nasdaq with a single prospectus. The framework sets a market‑capitalisation threshold of US$2 billion and aims to be operational by mid‑2026, offering harmonised rules and safe‑harbour provisions for forward‑looking statements. The initiative is intended to attract regional firms, broaden investor access, and generate new business for local service providers such as lawyers and accountants.

title: Geo Energy Resources secures up to US$100 million prepayment from Trafigura for coking coal off‑take at its newly acquired Harfa Taruna Mandiri
body: Geo Energy Resources announced it has agreed to a prepayment of US$50‑100 million from Trafigura to secure off‑take of all export volumes from its newly acquired miner Harfa Taruna Mandiri (HTM) in Central Kalimantan. The deal, together with a 15‑20 million‑tonne 2P reserve estimate and an expected 1.5 million tonnes of annual production, is intended to strengthen Geo Energy’s cash position and fund the ramp‑up of HTM’s operations. Geo Energy also signed a non‑binding MOU with East Wonders Indonesia, which plans to invest US$60 million to develop underground mining for HTM over the next 15 years, and the company’s shares closed 2.6 % higher at S$0.59 following the announcement.

title: Singtel’s special discounted shares will be transferred to individual CDP accounts after CPF Amendment Bill, giving the telco greater flexibility in corporate actions
body: The CPF Amendment Bill passed on May 7 will move Singtel’s special discounted shares (SDS) into holders’ own Central Depository (CDP) accounts in November, affecting about 615,000 Singaporeans. In the month prior, Singtel recorded roughly 60,000 walk‑in enquiries at 36 SingPost branches and 6,800 hotline calls as it prepares the transfer, and it plans to reach over 20,000 older, less‑digitally‑savvy SDS holders for additional assistance. As of April 30, 83,000 SDS holders (13% of all holders) had already sold their shares, with daily trading volumes averaging 4.5 million shares – about 11% of Singtel’s typical daily volume – and 90% of sellers opting for cash proceeds.

title: Genting Singapore reports 55% profit drop as Resorts World Sentosa faces higher costs and weaker travel demand
body: Genting Singapore, the operator of Resorts World Sentosa, posted a 55% decline in first‑quarter net profit to $65.2 million for the quarter ended 31 March 2026. Revenue fell 3% to $607.6 million, with gaming revenue down while non‑gaming revenue rose on higher visits to attractions such as Universal Studios Singapore and the Singapore Oceanarium. The results reflect higher energy, freight and logistics costs and weaker travel demand linked to the Iran‑US conflict, prompting the company to roll out new attractions, dining concepts and season passes at Resorts World Sentosa. Shares closed at 69 cents on May 12, up 1.47%.

title: Seatrium avoids prosecution in Singapore by agreeing to US$110 million penalty
body: Singapore-listed Seatrium secured High Court approval of a deferred prosecution agreement, requiring it to pay a US$110 million financial penalty, of which up to US$53 million can be offset against payments already made to Brazilian authorities, leaving a net payable of US$57 million (about S$73 million). The company said the penalty has been provisioned and will not materially affect earnings or net tangible asset per share for the financial year ending 31 December 2026. Shares rose 1.7 percent to $2.41 following the announcement on 24 April.

title: JustCo to raise up to S$100 million in SGX mainboard IPO targeting a S$459.9 million market cap
body: Home-grown flexible workspace operator JustCo announced it will list on the Singapore Exchange mainboard, offering 32.1 million shares at S$0.94 each, aiming to raise about S$100 million in gross proceeds and achieve a post‑listing market capitalisation of roughly S$459.9 million. The offering includes 74.3 million cornerstone shares and 25.8 million shares allocated to institutional investors, with net proceeds expected at S$92.2 million (up to S$97.1 million if the overallotment option is fully exercised), and the shares are set to begin trading on 22 May after the offer closes on 20 May. GIC, which invested in JustCo in 2018, remains the largest shareholder with a 29.1 % stake (to fall to 22.7 % after the IPO), while Frasers Property holds 22.5 % and will stay a key shareholder; JustCo reported FY2025 revenue of US$150.8 million and cash EBITDA of US$13.8 million.

title: Asti Holdings and Avi-Tech Holdings rally on strategic stake increases
body: Asti Holdings surged more than 120% in the past month, posting a 422.2% gain to a May‑12 closing price of S$0,188 and a market capitalisation of about S$137 million. Avi‑Tech Holdings rose about 70% over the same period, ending May 12 at S$0,295 with a market value of roughly S$49.6 million. The rallies were sparked by strategic investors – chief executive Eddie Ng bought 40 million Asti shares for S$3.6 million, becoming the controlling shareholder, while retail investor Global Wave Ventures acquired more than 50 million Avi‑Tech shares for a 29.9% stake. Analysts link the momentum to a broader global semiconductor rally and to demand from key customers such as Texas Instruments, but caution that thin trading and execution risk remain.

title: Institute of Singapore Chartered Accountants launches task force with Singapore Exchange to enhance financial reporting for SGX-listed firms
body: The Institute of Singapore Chartered Accountants (Isca) announced the Strengthening Financial Reporting Taskforce at the Value Unlock Forum on May 11, partnering with Singapore Exchange (SGX) to help SGX-listed companies improve disclosures and investor communication. The initiative is part of SGX's S$30 million Value Unlock programme, which includes the Equip and Elevate grants funded by the Monetary Authority of Singapore’s Financial Sector Development Fund. At the end of December 2025, Isca reported more than 43,000 members, including 23,920 Chartered Accountant (Singapore) charterholders and 9,722 student members.

title: Lum Chang Holdings’ valuation surges after spinoff of Lum Chang Creations
body: Lum Chang Holdings, the long‑time construction group listed on SGX, saw its valuation and returns improve after spinning off its high‑margin urban‑revitalisation unit, Lum Chang Creations, which listed on the Catalist board in July 2025. The newly listed Lum Chang Creations posted a half‑year net profit of S$11 million, ROE in the mid‑30 % range and a share price gain of about 292 % from its IPO price. Following the spin‑off, Lum Chang Holdings distributed special dividends to shareholders in early 2026, reflecting the stronger earnings profile of the group.

title: JustCo files Singapore mainboard prospectus as it targets expansion with US$104 million cash
body: JustCo, the Singapore‑founded flexible workspace operator, lodged its preliminary prospectus with the Monetary Authority of Singapore on May 7 as it seeks a mainboard listing on the Singapore Exchange. The company reported a net profit of US$2.7 million for 2025, reversing losses of US$10.1 million in 2024 and US$12.5 million in 2023, with revenue rising to US$150.8 million and occupancy reaching 84 percent. It holds about US$104 million in cash, carries no external bank debt, and has secured cornerstone investors to subscribe for 74.3 million shares, while DBS Bank and UBS serve as joint issue managers and global coordinators and Maybank Securities acts as an underwriter.

title: Riverstone leads iEdge Singapore Next 50 gains as Singapore market rises
body: Singapore's Straits Times Index rose 0.4% to 4,942.77, with OCBC Bank leading the blue‑chip gainers up 2.6% to $22.50, while DBS Bank and UOB also posted modest advances. In the iEdge Singapore Next 50 Index, Riverstone was the top performer, climbing 7.2% to 82 cents despite a 27.1% drop in first‑quarter net profit to RM41.1 million (S$13.3 million) from RM56.4 million. Seatrium was the worst STI constituent, falling 3% to $2.23, and China Aviation Oil recorded the biggest loss in the broader market, down 5.7% to $1.98. Overall, losers outnumbered gainers 340 to 279 with $2.6 billion traded.

title: Lendlease Global Commercial REIT reports 95.3% occupancy and 12.2% retail rental reversion in Q3
body: Lendlease Global Commercial Reit reported portfolio occupancy rising to 95.3% from 94.9% in the prior quarter and a 12.2% retail rental reversion for the third quarter ended March 31. The REIT completed the acquisition of the remaining 30% stake in PLQ Mall, achieving full control, and with PLQ Mall’s contribution year‑to‑date tenant sales grew 17.6% and shopper visits rose 13.7% versus a year earlier; on a like‑for‑like basis excluding PLQ Mall, sales and visits were up 2.5% and 5.2%. Gearing stood at 38.7% (37.5% pro forma), weighted average cost of debt remained about 2.9%, interest coverage was 1.8×, and the manager issued S$120 million of 4.28% perpetual securities to refinance S$200 million due in June, with S$611 million of debt facilities available.

title: SGX RegCo queries Mary Chia Holdings' ability to continue as a going concern amid Fullink Capital insolvency proceedings
body: SGX RegCo asked Mary Chia Holdings and its sponsor to assess whether the company can remain a going concern after Fullink Capital launched insolvency proceedings against Mary Chia, its subsidiary Organica International Holdings, founder Ho Yow Ping and CFO Su Jun Ming. Mary Chia’s board said on May 14 that after reviewing cash flow, liquidity and legal exposure, it can continue operating and meet obligations, noting its shares fell 4.4% to 2.2 cents and that the disputed loan amount of $902,640 (original $350,000 loan) remains unresolved. The firm highlighted support from controlling shareholders Suki Sushi and Ms Ho, is exploring fundraising and will address the case in a court conference scheduled for May 21.

title: OCBC Bank posts 5% income rise as it moves to acquire HSBC Indonesia wealth assets
body: OCBC Bank reported first‑quarter total income of $3.83 billion, up 5% year‑on‑year, with net profit of $1.97 billion and wealth‑management contributing 39% of income, and announced it will acquire parts of HSBC’s wealth and premier banking portfolio in Indonesia. UOB posted a 6% decline in total income to $3.42 billion and a 4% drop in net profit to $1.43 billion while targeting to double its wealth income by 2030. Co‑working operator JustCo filed a preliminary prospectus for an IPO after turning a net profit of US$2.7 million in 2025 on revenue of US$150.8 million, and other Singapore‑listed firms disclosed results: StarHub’s profit fell 81.3% to $5.9 million on revenue $507.3 million; SBS Transit’s revenue rose 4.8% to $391.8 million while profit slipped to $15.6 million; Venture Corp’s revenue grew 1.9% to $628.5 million with net profit $56.3 million; Jardine Matheson’s shares rose as it considers selling its car‑dealership business owned by Jardine Cycle & Carriage, and Hongkong Land, a Jardine Matheson subsidiary, saw its share price rise on speculation of a bid for Marina One; Singapore Airlines, holding a 25.1% stake in Air India, will report results on May 14.

title: CGS International aims to boost Chinese listings on SGX from five to up to 25 in coming years
body: CGS International, a wholly owned subsidiary of state‑owned broker China Galaxy Securities, said it is in talks with Chinese firms to increase the number of China‑linked listings on the Singapore Exchange from the current five to as many as 25 over the next two to three years. The firm previously estimated only about five Chinese or Hong Kong companies would list via dual listings or share placements, but now calls that figure conservative. It is targeting mid‑sized companies valued at roughly US$500 million to US$1 billion that need non‑renminbi funding and a regional branding platform, rather than mega‑caps such as Alibaba or BYD. The push follows CGS’s 2024 full acquisition of its joint venture with Malaysia’s CIMB Group, positioning the subsidiary to source higher‑quality issuers for SGX.

title: Mary Chia Holdings faces insolvency proceedings over $902,640 loan dispute with Fullink Capital
body: Mary Chia Holdings and its wholly owned subsidiary Organica International Holdings are subject to insolvency proceedings initiated by creditor Fullink Capital over an outstanding loan of $902,640. The dispute stems from an original $350,000 loan to Organica guaranteed by Mary Chia, with Mary Chia proposing a revised payment of about $354,379, which Fullink rejected on March 25. Mary Chia reported that revenue for the nine months ended 31 Dec 2025 fell to $11.1 million from $31 million a year earlier, net profit shrank to $28,000, cash fell to $116,000 and borrowings rose to $3.5 million, prompting a 5.7 million‑share placement at 3.5 cents raising roughly $200,000. A case‑management conference is set for 6 May, and Mary Chia seeks a temporary suspension of the proceedings while it pursues a court declaration on the enforceability of the claims.

title: KTL Global and Sasseur Real Estate Investment Trust implicated in convictions for false and insider trading
body: The Monetary Authority of Singapore announced that former OCBC Securities trading representative Tan Chun Yong received a 10‑week prison term for abetting false trading in the shares of KTL Global, where he helped create a false appearance of active trading between November 2014 and September 2015. KTL Global’s former CEO Tan Kheng Yeow was earlier found guilty of conspiring to inflate the share price, and the company had previously failed to meet the Singapore Exchange’s new minimum trading price requirement in 2014. In a separate case, Xie Jianfeng, a former finance manager of an entity linked to the manager of Sasseur Real Estate Investment Trust, was fined S$200,000 and ordered to disgorge S$89,000 after profiting about S$224,000 from insider trades of Sasseur Real Estate Investment Trust units based on non‑public FY2020 results. He also voluntarily contributed S$135,000 to charity, and the investigations were conducted jointly by MAS and the Commercial Affairs Department following referrals from the Singapore Exchange.

title: Singapore Airlines flight SQ321 underscores rising safety incidents amid higher fuel‑price pressures in Asia‑Pacific
body: The Civil Aviation Authority of Singapore reported that safety incidents in the Asia‑Pacific region have risen sharply, with accident rates increasing from 0.78 per million departures in 2023 to 1.62 in 2024 and fatalities climbing from 72 to 186. Turbulence‑related accidents grew from two in 2023 to eight in 2024, while runway incursions at Changi Airport rose from zero in 2023 to two in 2024 and three in 2025, all involving foreign carriers. Singapore Airlines was directly affected when flight SQ321 suffered a turbulence accident that left one passenger dead and dozens injured. The regulator urged airlines facing higher fuel costs to maintain essential safety expenditures despite financial pressures.

title: Investigation Report May Lead to Court Action Against Singapore Airlines Over SQ321 Turbulence
body: A report released on May 19 found that a possible weather‑radar defect may have caused the severe turbulence on SQ321, injuring 79 passengers and crew and killing one person. The radar manufacturer said no malfunction evidence was found, while pilots reported no weather indications on the radar before the event. Legal experts say the findings could prompt unavoidable court litigation against Singapore Airlines, although the airline’s counsel stresses the report is intended to improve aviation safety rather than assign blame.

title: Grab and ComfortDelGro expand autonomous shuttle trials in Singapore
body: Grab and ComfortDelGro have begun passenger trials of autonomous shuttles in Singapore, with Grab reporting over 3,800 rides and ComfortDelGro reporting 700 invite‑only rides. The shuttles used by Grab are developed by AV firm WeRide, while ComfortDelGro’s vehicles are built by Pony.ai. Private bus operators A&S Transit and Westpoint Transit, both described as private bus companies, voiced concerns about the technology’s ability to handle complex on‑board situations and route changes. The Land Transport Authority plans to purchase six autonomous buses for trial on routes 400 and 191, indicating a broader push toward AV deployment despite regulatory and safety challenges.

title: Singapore Telecommunications posts 12% rise in annual underlying profit and raises dividend
body: Singapore Telecommunications (Singtel) reported a 12% increase in annual underlying profit for the year ended March 2026, with underlying net profit of S$2.77 billion, missing the Visible Alpha consensus of S$2.82 billion. Post‑tax profit contributions from regional associates—including India's Bharti Airtel, Thailand's Advanced Info Service (AIS) and Indonesia's Telkomsel—rose 11% to S$1.96 billion, underpinning the profit growth. The group’s unit Optus saw operating revenue increase 2% on postpaid price hikes and a regional network‑sharing arrangement. Singtel declared a final dividend of 10.3 Singapore cents per share, up from 10 cents a year earlier.

title: Singamas Container Holdings faces US price‑fixing charges and requests one‑day trading halt
body: The U.S. Justice Department alleges Singamas Container Holdings and other container makers conspired to restrict output and fix the price of dry containers from November 2019 through at least January 2024. The alleged scheme roughly doubled container prices between 2019 and 2021, boosting manufacturers’ profits about one hundredfold during the COVID‑19 pandemic. Singamas, a listed subsidiary of Pacific International Lines, said it has not been served with any legal process, has engaged external counsel and will maintain normal operations while requesting a one‑day trading halt. CIMC said it is monitoring the matter but has not been served with any documentation.

title: Singtel seeks regulator clarity on possible acquisition of M1 after Simba deal collapse
body: Singtel said it will seek regulator guidance on whether it can take part in further consolidation of Singapore’s telecom market following the collapse of Simba’s proposed acquisition of M1. Keppel, the parent company of M1, announced it will let its sale and purchase agreement with Simba lapse and remain open to new buyers for the telco. At the same time, Singtel, after releasing its full‑year financial results for the year ended 31 March 2026, reiterated its interest in acquiring M1 and indicated it is open to a minority‑stake partner for its Australian subsidiary Optus. The Infocomm Media Development Authority has suspended its assessment of Simba’s acquisition proposal pending investigation into alleged use of unassigned radio‑frequency bands.

title: OCBC Securities and Sasseur REIT face Singapore regulatory penalties
body: Singapore's Monetary Authority announced that OCBC Securities trading representative Tan Chun Yong received a 10‑week jail term for aiding false trading in KTL shares through six unauthorised accounts. In a separate insider‑trading case, Xie, former finance manager of Sasseur Commercial Management Group Co., Ltd., a related corporation of Sasseur Asset Management Pte Ltd, the manager of Sasseur REIT, was fined $200,000, contributed $134,720 to charity and paid $88,852.68 disgorgement after profiting about $223,572.68 from non‑public FY2020 results. Additionally, MAS revoked the major payment institution licence of Bsquared Technology Pte Ltd on 14 May 2026, barring it from providing digital payment token services.

title: Australia's Tuas shares tumble 10% after terminating M1 acquisition
body: Australia's Tuas, the owner of Simba, announced on May 22 that its agreement to acquire M1 was terminated, releasing both Tuas and Keppel—M1’s parent company—from their obligations under the sales and purchase agreement. The termination follows a long‑stop date that had been extended to May 21 and comes amid an IMDA investigation into Simba’s use of unassigned radio‑frequency bands. Tuas shares fell nearly 10 percent in early Sydney trading to A$2.08 (US$1.49) after the announcement, adding to a more than 60 percent plunge on the previous Monday. The company said it will keep shareholders updated on the regulator’s probe.

title: CapitaLand Integrated raises payout by 40% as United Overseas Bank cuts dividend
body: Capital Group's Dividend Watch shows Singaporean dividend payouts surged 41.3% YoY to $455 million in Q1 2026, driven by only two listed companies. CapitaLand Integrated increased its dividend by two‑fifths (about 40%) while United Overseas Bank announced a dividend cut for Q2 amid lower profitability. Capital Group cautioned that the strong 34.7% core dividend growth may not persist, noting the limited sample and broader global dividend growth of 8.2% to $536.6 billion.

title: Singamas Container Holdings CEO Teo Siong Seng Takes Leave Amid US Price‑Fixing Indictment
body: Singamas Container Holdings CEO and chairman Teo Siong Seng will take a leave of absence from his roles at the Singapore Business Federation, the Singapore Economic Resilience Taskforce and Enterprise Singapore. The leave follows his indictment by the US Department of Justice for allegedly conspiring to restrict output and fix prices of dry containers, a scheme the Justice Department says ran from November 2019 to at least January 2024. The conspiracy allegedly caused standard container prices to double between 2019 and 2021, boosting container manufacturers’ profits by roughly 100‑fold during the COVID‑19 pandemic. Teo told the Ministry of Trade and Industry the leave is to focus on addressing the US indictment.

title: Keppel's aborted M1 acquisition triggers share swings and broader market updates
body: Tuas Limited, the Australian‑listed owner of Simba, terminated its sale‑and‑purchase agreement to acquire M1 from Keppel, ending Simba’s $1.43 billion bid and prompting Keppel’s shares to rise 5.11 % to $10.91 while Singtel fell 4.97 % to $4.59. Singtel reported a second‑half net profit of $2.2 billion, down 20.9 % YoY on revenue of about $7.3 billion, and said it is seeking regulator approval to participate in any future telco consolidation. City Developments Limited appointed Kwek Leng Peck as vice‑chairman, posted a weaker Q1 2026 Singapore property sale of 242 units worth $609.6 million versus 795 units a year earlier, and its shares rose 3.94 % to $8.17. Other market moves included Gardenia Foods’ plan to retrench 141 staff as production shifts to Malaysia, QAF’s 15 % YoY profit rise to $40.3 million, JustCo’s SGX debut at 77.5 cents (‑17.6 % from IPO price), Hour Glass’s net profit of $103.8 million up 39 %, and Frencken’s profit falling 20.2 % to $8 million.

title: AEM Holdings shares surge 450% in 2026 as AI chip testing demand drives revenue outlook
body: AEM Holdings, a Singapore-listed provider of testing systems for high‑performance AI chips, has seen its shares climb about 450% from under $2 in January to $9.56 at the close of trading on 22 May 2026. The company raised its 2026 revenue guidance by roughly 20% to a range of $550 million‑$600 million as it diversifies beyond Intel, adds a second major AI/HPC customer expected to overtake Intel as its largest client, and secures memory‑chip customers Samsung Electronics, Micron Technology and SK Hynix. A partnership with ASE Technology Holding, which invested about $12 million in AEM, is intended to expand AEM’s testing capacity for AI and advanced memory chips and to reach more global AI‑chip makers.

title: Jardine Matheson Holdings to acquire I-MED Radiology Network for $3.11 billion
body: Jardine Matheson Holdings Limited has agreed to buy 100% of I-MED Radiology Network for an enterprise value of $3.11 billion (AU$3.4 billion), valuing the core business at about 11.5 times forecast adjusted EBITDA for the year ending June 2026. I-MED operates 215 diagnostic imaging clinics across Australia and New Zealand, handling more than 7 million patient procedures annually with a network of over 500 radiologists. The acquisition will be funded with cash on the balance sheet and debt, and JMH said its underlying earnings‑per‑share and dividend guidance for 2026 remain unchanged. JMH also moved to take full control of Mandarin Oriental International Limited by acquiring the remaining minority stake in early 2026.

title: JustCo raises S$100 million in IPO as Singapore Exchange eyes close to 30 listings in 2026
body: Singapore Exchange reported that the local IPO market generated about S$3 billion in proceeds last year and is on track for nearly 30 listings in 2026. On May 22, Singapore Exchange welcomed its third mainboard offering of the year when homegrown flexible‑workspace provider JustCo raised S$100 million to fund overseas expansion, marking the exchange’s fifth listing of the year. JustCo, which is backed by Singapore sovereign‑wealth fund GIC, said the S$6.5 billion Equity Market Development Programme and improved liquidity, with trading volumes doubling over 18 months, helped boost confidence in the listing.

title: SATS reports record $6.35 billion revenue as Middle East conflict drives cargo surge
body: SATS said its FY2026 revenue reached a record $6.35 billion, a 9 % rise from the prior year, driven largely by its gateway services. Gateway services contributed $4.95 billion, about 78 % of total revenue, up 10.8 % year‑on‑year, while food‑service revenue grew 2.9 %. The company attributed the strong performance to its extensive network of 225 locations in 27 countries and recent capacity investments such as the Bulk Unitisation Programme Handling Centre at Changi Airport. Logistics for reconstruction shipments to the Middle East were handled by Worldwide Flight Services, a SATS subsidiary, underscoring the group’s ability to capture cargo redirected by the Israel‑US‑Iran conflict.

title: Eurosports Global convicted after price‑manipulation scheme inflates its share price
body: Eurosports Global was the subject of a price‑manipulation scheme that inflated its closing share price by 2% to 22% over 77 trading days between 24 February 2017 and 12 January 2018. The scheme, carried out by trader Wong Chow Lin and his broker Gillian Isabel Siow Siang Sok of CIMB Securities (Singapore), allowed Wong to avoid margin calls on 31 days, reduce their impact on 16 days, and improve margin valuations on 30 days. Wong received a four‑week jail sentence, while Siow was fined S$135,000.

title: Koh Brothers Eco Engineering proposes transfer from SGX Catalist to mainboard
body: Koh Brothers Eco Engineering, a subsidiary of construction and property group Koh Brothers, has filed an application to move its shares from the SGX Catalist board to the mainboard. The company, listed on Catalist since 27 February 2006, noted that a mainboard listing could improve liquidity, attract institutional investors and enhance its valuation, with its shares closing at S$0,132, down 2.2% before the announcement. Koh Brothers holds a 54.8% stake in the unit and the group reported a total order book of about S$1.1 billion across engineering, construction, bio‑refinery and renewable‑energy segments as of 31 December 2025.

title: Pacific International Lines executive chairman Teo Siong Seng takes leave of absence amid US price‑fixing probe
body: Pacific International Lines (PIL) announced that its executive chairman and director Teo Siong Seng will take a leave of absence effective 8 June, following U.S. accusations of a dry‑container output‑restriction and price‑fixing scheme. Teo also expanded his leave from other roles, including chairman of the Singapore Business Federation (SBF) and Pro‑Chancellor of the National University of Singapore (NUS), with those absences taking effect on 1 June and his SBF chairmanship ending on 24 June. The company said the temporary leadership change is intended to allow Teo to address the matter and to protect the interests of the organisations involved.

title: Trek 2000 International posts 12‑fold profit jump as Azure Capital takes 7.3% stake
body: Trek 2000 International reported FY2025 net profit of US$4.6 million, a nearly 12‑fold increase from the prior year’s US$335 k, while revenue slipped 1.1% to US$19.6 million. Its AIoT division contributed 93.2% of sales and the company expects more than US$15 million from a new AI‑powered aviation solution with partner Aboard AI through FY2027. Azure Capital acquired 22,074,000 ordinary shares of Trek, representing about 7.3% of the issued share capital, for over S$2.6 million at S$0.12 per share, reducing Ron Sim’s holding to 2% and ending his status as a substantial shareholder. Following the announcement, Trek’s shares jumped 28.9% to close at S$0,205.

title: Trek 2000 International secures Azure Capital as new substantial shareholder, shares surge 29%
body: Trek 2000 International announced that Singapore‑based fund manager Azure Capital became a direct substantial shareholder after buying 22.1 million shares, about 7.3 % of the company, for 12 cents each ($2.65 million). The purchase lifted Trek 2000’s share price 10.5 % to 12 cents on May 12 and nearly 29 % to 20 cents after the May 28 filing. For FY 2025, Trek 2000 reported net profit attributable to shareholders of US$4.6 million, a 1,275.8 % increase year‑on‑year, driven by AI and IoT businesses that now account for over 90 % of revenue. Ron Sim reduced his holding from about 9.3 % to 2 % and withdrew all legal claims, removing a lingering dispute.

title: Surrey Hills Holdings former CEO Pang Gek Teng charged with embezzling S$242,738
body: Former CEO and founder Pang Gek Teng was charged in Singapore State Courts with twelve offences, including nine counts of cheating, one count of forgery, one count of attempted cheating and one count of criminal breach of trust. The charges relate to the alleged misappropriation of S$242,738.11 from Surrey Hills Holdings between 3 April 2023 and 28 February 2024, as well as fraudulent schemes that duped victims of more than S$400,000 and involved a forged S$20,000 invoice from AC Global Consulting. Pang was dismissed from Surrey Hills Holdings on 26 March 2023 and faces up to 10 years’ jail for cheating or forgery and up to 20 years for criminal breach of trust, with the case adjourned to 10 July.

title: Sats leads STI gains as Singapore market posts 10.8% YTD total return
body: The Straits Times Index delivered a 10.8% total return in the first five months of 2026, reaching a fresh record high of 5,102.07 on May 25. Sats, the provider of gateway services and food solutions, posted the strongest May performance among STI constituents with a 16.7% price gain, while Venture, a technology solutions provider, added 11.1% in the same month. Frasers Logistics & Commercial Trust was the top‑performing REIT, rising 4.2% after agreeing to acquire four logistics and industrial properties in Europe for €294.9 million, and DBS Group recorded S$637 million of net institutional inflows, reducing its cumulative 2026 outflow to S$1.47 billion. UMS Integration led the iEdge Next 50 Liquidity Index with a 28.4% price jump, driven by a 20% revenue increase to S$69.4 million and a 43% profit rise to S$14 million in Q1 FY2026.

title: Mapletree Investments posts 25.7% profit rise to $285.6 million in FY25/26
body: Mapletree Investments reported a 25.7% year‑on‑year increase in profit after tax and minority interest to $285.6 million for the fiscal year ended 31 March 2026, with recurring PATMI climbing to $622.8 million. The group recycled $4.2 billion of capital through strategic divestments, including over $2.5 billion monetised by its private funds and $1 billion divested by its three REITs—Mapletree Logistics Trust, Mapletree Industrial Trust and Mapletree Pan Asia Commercial Trust. Assets under management grew to $76.2 billion, driven by a $32.4 billion logistics portfolio (42.5% of AUM) and $63.4 billion in its four core sectors, while $5.4 billion of projects—$2.6 billion in logistics—remain under development.

title: Singapore Kitchen Equipment and subsidiary Q'son Kitchen Equipment face fraud and falsification charges
body: Singapore Kitchen Equipment, which operates and wholly owns subsidiary Q'son Kitchen Equipment, has been charged with multiple fraud‑related offences. The CEO Chua Chwee Choo, former CFO Chow Mei Ling and senior manager Koh Sai Eng are accused of conspiring between February and March 2021 to misrepresent to auditor BDO that bonus payments of about S$740,000 were paid to Q'son employees in January 2020. Prosecutors allege Chow also omitted eight payments totalling roughly S$1.4 million for 2018‑2019 and later falsified entries to include them in Q'son’s 2020 accounts, resulting in more than 100 falsified payment vouchers and false profitability statements for FY2018‑FY2020.

title: Singapore government funds S$450 monthly salary boost and S$2,000 sign‑on bonus increase for bus drivers, affecting SBS Transit, Go‑Ahead Singapore, SMRT and Tower Transit
body: The Singapore government will fund a S$450 per month increase in starting salaries and a S$2,000 rise in sign‑on bonuses for new Singaporean and permanent‑resident bus drivers starting Jan 1 2027.
