The four public bus operators – SBS Transit, Go‑Ahead Singapore, SMRT and Tower Transit – will implement the adjustments, which raise first‑year earnings by about S$600 and lift average monthly pay to over S$4,000 including overtime and allowances. Operators have already been offering sign‑on bonuses up to S$20,000 (SBS Transit, Go‑Ahead Singapore), S$33,000 (SMRT) and S$10,000 (Tower Transit, up from S$7,200), and the new funding aims to improve retention as the proportion of local bus captains fell to 41 % in 2025.

title: Singapore Kitchen Equipment executives charged in accounting scandal but retain positions
body: Singapore Kitchen Equipment disclosed that its chief executive Chua Chwee Choo and senior manager Koh Sai Eng will remain in their roles despite being charged under the Penal Code and the Securities and Futures Act for alleged falsification of accounts. The charges stem from a February‑March 2021 conspiracy to make false representations to auditor BDO about bonuses paid by Singapore Kitchen Equipment’s subsidiary Q’son Kitchen Equipment, including falsifying more than 100 payment vouchers and omitting eight payments totalling about $1.4 million from Q’son Kitchen Equipment’s 2018‑2019 accounts. The trio face a total of 16 charges – Chow Mei Ling with 12 (including eight amalgamated) and Chua and Koh each with two amalgamated charges – and the company, whose shares have been suspended since August 2021, says the court proceedings will not disrupt operations.

title: Singapore Airlines in early talks to purchase at least 50 wide‑body jets from Airbus and Boeing
body: Singapore Airlines is in early-stage discussions with Airbus and Boeing to acquire at least 50 wide‑body aircraft, evaluating the 400‑seat Boeing 777X and the Airbus A350‑1000. The carrier, a major long‑haul jet buyer, regularly reviews fleet renewal plans and aims to expand capacity despite higher oil prices affecting rivals. Airbus is also weighing a larger A350‑2000 model, while Boeing has agreed to revisit studies for a bigger plane after Emirates ordered additional 777X jets.

title: DBS recommends OCBC, Singtel and Venture as top picks ahead of a post‑World Cup Singapore market rebound
body: DBS analysts note that the FIFA World Cup (June 11 – July 19) typically weakens SGX trading, creating a tactical buying window. They single out blue‑chip dividend payers OCBC, Singtel and Venture as top picks, and add City Developments and UOL for second‑half catalysts. In the semiconductor arena, DBS favours UMS over AEM and highlights InnoTek and MetaOptics as AI‑related opportunities. The brokerage maintains its year‑end STI target at 5,250, expects the index to stay above 4,700 with a 50 % probability, and cites historical World‑Cup trading drops of –24.38 % (2002), –47.84 % (2006), –17.09 % (2010), –29.67 % (2014) and –5.21 % (2018).

title: JustCo founder buys 500,000 shares as post‑IPO price slides
body: JustCo founder and chief executive Kong Wan Sing purchased a total of 500,000 shares on the open market—200,000 on June 3 at 65.5 cents each and 300,000 on June 4 at 69.4 cents each—raising his direct holding to 812,500 shares and, together with a deemed interest in 89.7 million shares, bringing his total stake to about 18.5 percent. The purchases come as JustCo’s shares, which debuted at the IPO price of 94 cents on May 22, opened at 83.5 cents (11.5 % below) and closed at 66.5 cents on June 5, while DBS Bank has bought 5.3 million shares under a price‑stabilisation mechanism. The company, which reported its first profit of US$2.7 million in 2025, holds roughly $135 million in cash, no debt, and is backed by GIC (22.7 % stake) and Frasers Property (17.6 % stake) as it plans to expand from 54 to 154 workspace centres by 2029.

title: Lum Chang Creations postpones bonus‑share listing pending placement timing
body: Lum Chang Creations (LCC) announced it will postpone applying to the Singapore Exchange for the listing and quotation of its proposed one‑for‑one bonus shares until the pending placement is completed. The Catalist‑listed subsidiary of Lum Chang Holdings (LCH) had received in‑principal SGX approval for a transfer to the mainboard on Feb 13 and shareholders approved the transfer and bonus issue at an extraordinary general meeting on May 25. Because the placement timing remains uncertain, LCC will wait for further clarity before setting a record date, and its shares fell 2.3% to S$0.84, while LCH’s shares were flat at S$0.53.

title: Four companies added and four removed from iEdge Singapore Next 50 indices in June review
body: AEM, Top Glove, UI Boustead Real Estate Investment Trust and PC Partner Group were added to the iEdge Singapore Next 50 and iEdge Singapore Next 50 Weighted indices in the June review. They replace SingPost, Digital Core Reit, Wee Hur and China Sunsine Chemical, with the changes taking effect on June 22. Following the review, technology‑related firms now represent about 26.2% of the iEdge Singapore Next 50 Liquidity Weighted Index (up from 16.6%), and the index posted a 12.3% total return from January to May 2026 versus 10.8% for the Straits Times Index.

title: SingPost expands SingPost@MyBlock to four estates and launches a S$30 million automated sorting hub
body: SingPost is rolling out its SingPost@MyBlock service to four additional housing estates—Bukit Batok, Bukit Panjang, Marine Parade and Upper Boon Keng—while maintaining its existing network of about 40 post offices and 786 postboxes. The postal group also opened a S$30 million automated parcel‑sorting facility at its Regional eCommerce Logistics Hub in Tampines, featuring a 3D sorter and an intelligent flexi sorter that together raise small‑ and medium‑parcel capacity from 100,000 to 300,000 parcels per day and lift total daily throughput to 400,000 parcels. Automation cuts processing time by up to three hours, reduces staffing needs from roughly 300 workers to 150‑200 (mainly temporary staff), and is part of a broader strategy to lower operating expenses by more than 10 percent. The upgrade includes 40 electric automated guided vehicles, three larger autonomous vehicles, 327 output chutes and a scanner system that records parcel dimensions and weight.

title: Singtel leads Singapore blue‑chip buybacks in early 2026, with OCBC and Keppel also repurchasing shares
body: Over the first five months of 2026, Singapore’s primary‑listed companies repurchased S$1.26 billion of shares, with Singapore Telecommunications, OCBC and Keppel Ltd accounting for the bulk of the activity. Singtel, the largest buyer, lifted its FY2026 ordinary dividend to S$0,185 per share (up 9% YoY) on an underlying net profit of S$2.8 billion and funded the buyback by selling a 0.8% stake in Airtel for S$1.5 billion, improving net‑debt gearing to 23.3%; OCBC repurchased shares under a S$2.5 billion capital‑return plan after posting record Q1 2026 total income of S$3.8 billion and net profit of S$2.0 billion while maintaining a 50% payout guidance; Keppel’s buyback rests on a planned S$2–3 billion non‑core asset monetisation after a quarter that turned to free‑cash inflow and saw asset‑management fees rise 13% to S$108 million. The analysis shows Singtel and OCBC’s repurchases are backed by disclosed earnings and cash, whereas Keppel’s buyback depends on future monetisation and less transparent cash generation.

title: Genting Singapore posts 32% profit decline in FY2025 and maintains flat S$0.04 dividend
body: Genting Singapore, which owns and runs Resorts World Sentosa (RWS), reported FY2025 revenue of S$2.5 billion, down 3.1% YoY, with net profit falling 32.6% to S$390.3 million. Gaming revenue dropped 5.8% to S$1.6 billion while non‑gaming rose 1.9% to S$832.3 million, and adjusted EBITDA fell 15% to S$815.8 million. The company kept its FY2025 dividend at S$0.04 per share (≈6.6% yield) despite free cash flow plunging 51.7% to S$211.3 million, funded by S$3.2 billion of cash and a 36.9% increase in capex to S$578.7 million for the RWS 2.0 transformation. In 1Q2026 revenue slipped 3% to S$607.6 million, with gaming down 8% and non‑gaming up 8%, underscoring the need for a gaming recovery to sustain the payout.

title: Shopee cuts Singapore jobs amid Sea’s AI‑driven restructuring
body: Shopee announced layoffs in its Singapore headquarters, affecting software engineers and other product and engineering staff as part of a regular review of staffing needs. The cuts are linked to Sea, Shopee’s parent company, which is pursuing an artificial‑intelligence strategy that it says could unlock a trillion‑dollar market valuation. In the first quarter of 2026 Sea reported operating expenses up 43.4% year‑on‑year to almost US$2.6 billion (S$3.3 billion) and cost of revenue rising 51.7% to US$4 billion. Net income grew 6.7% to US$438.2 million and adjusted EBITDA increased 9.3% to US$1 billion.

title: Tiong Woon Corp highlighted as undervalued heavy‑lift crane operator with strong margin expansion
body: Tiong Woon Corp (TWC) is the only publicly listed heavy‑lift crane company in Southeast Asia and is ranked the 15th‑largest crane operator worldwide with a fleet of 579 cranes, 359 haulage assets, 7 tugboats and 9 barges. Analysts note its stock has risen 79% to S$1.04 over the past year while gross profit margins improved from 38.5% in 1HFY25 to 42.9% in 1HFY26, supporting a fair‑value estimate of S$1.30 based on a 12× forward PE. The company’s recent acquisition of Mammoet’s assets in Thailand and deployment of high‑tonnage cranes to projects such as Saudi Arabia’s NEOM and Indian petrochemical plants are cited as drivers of higher‑margin overseas earnings. With a low net‑debt balance sheet and cash‑generative model that shields it from tender‑price and labour‑cost pressures, analysts view TWC as a discounted entry point despite its small‑cap illiquidity.

title: AEM Holdings, Top Glove Corporation join SGX Next 50 as four stocks exit
body: AEM Holdings, Top Glove Corporation, UI Boustead REIT and PC Partner Group will be added to the iEdge Singapore Next 50 Index after its June 2026 quarterly review. They replace Singapore Post, Digital Core REIT, Wee Hur Holdings and China Sunsine Chemical Holdings, with the changes taking effect on 22 June. The remaining 45 constituents recorded a combined average daily traded value of S$298 million in the year to 9 June, up from S$121 million in the same period in 2025, and the index posted a total return of 12.3% from January to May 2026. SGX said the technology sector’s weight in the liquidity‑weighted version of the index will rise to 26.2% (from 15.8% in the standard index), while S‑REITs will account for 29.7% of the liquidity‑weighted index versus 35.9% in the standard version, with telecommunications and utilities weights falling to 2.9% and 1.9% respectively.

title: Three SGX-listed firms boost dividends backed by strong cash positions
body: SIA Engineering Company (SGX: S59), an MRO specialist, posted a net cash position of S$559.4 million and lifted its FY2026 total dividend 22.2% to S$0.11 per share, with revenue of S$1.4 billion and net profit of S$168.9 million. iFAST Corporation (SGX: AIY), a wealth‑management fintech, held S$384.4 million net cash, surged its interim dividend 56.3% to S$0,0250 and guided a full‑year payout of at least S$0,1050, while 1Q2026 revenue jumped 44.5% to S$154.5 million and net profit rose 47.3% to S$28.0 million. BRC Asia (SGX: BEC), a steel‑reinforcement specialist, reported a net cash balance of S$52.0 million, increased its interim dividend 33.3% to S$0.08 per share and turned six‑month free cash flow positive to S$61.0 million after a prior negative, supported by revenue of S$931.0 million and profit of S$52.0 million. BRC’s performance was aided by its August 2025 acquisition of the Malaysian subsidiary Southern Steel Mesh, while iFAST noted working‑capital timing effects in its digital‑banking EzRemit division.

title: CapitaLand Integrated Commercial Trust vs CapitaLand Ascendas REIT: Which Offers Better Value
body: CapitaLand Integrated Commercial Trust (CICT) and CapitaLand Ascendas REIT (CLAR) are compared as Singapore’s largest REITs, both sponsored by CapitaLand Investment Limited. CICT trades around S$2.28 with a trailing annualised distribution yield of 5.1% and leverages 38.5%, while CLAR trades around S$2.45 with a 6.1% yield and 42% leverage expected to fall to about 37.3% after a S$903.5 million equity raise. Since 2021 CICT has consistently raised its distributions, whereas CLAR’s distribution per unit has slipped slightly even as its FY2025 distributable income rose 1.4%; CICT’s portfolio is Singapore‑focused retail and office assets, while CLAR holds industrial, logistics and data‑centre assets with 33% of value outside Singapore. A 1 % rise in interest rates would add S$24.1 million to CICT’s finance costs and would cut CLAR’s interest coverage ratio to 2.7 times from 3.5 times, highlighting differing refinancing pressures.

title: Micro-Mechanics delivers strong Q3 FY2026 results and maintains over 700% cumulative dividend return since 2003
body: Micro-Mechanics (SGX: 5DD) has paid a total of 137.9 cents per share in dividends since its 2003 listing, delivering a cumulative dividend return of more than 700%. In 3QFY2026 the company reported revenue of S$18.6 million, up 16.2% YoY, with gross profit of S$9.6 million (+18.9%) and operating profit of S$5.2 million (+24.6%). Net profit rose 18.8% to S$3.8 million and the consumable tools segment contributed S$14.4 million (77.6% of sales) growing 20.9% YoY, while China accounted for 34.8% of nine‑month revenue, increasing over 25% YoY. Gross margins stayed above 50% for three quarters, free cash flow slipped to S$2.8 million for the quarter, and the balance sheet held S$25.7 million of net cash with zero debt, supporting a S$2 million capex plan for the second half of FY2026.

title: DBS faces higher exposure to Indonesia and India as Singapore banks show uneven regional risk
body: A UOB Kay Hian report notes that DBS Group Holdings derives 7.4% of its 2025 income from Indonesia and India, making it the most exposed Singapore bank to the 7.4% depreciation of the Indonesian rupiah and 6% fall of the Indian rupee against the Singapore dollar in the first five months of 2026. OCBC Bank and United Overseas Bank also have exposure to Indonesia, but OCBC’s exposure is partly offset by stronger earnings from Malaysia where the ringgit gained 1.6% versus the Singapore dollar, and the broker maintains a target price of $26.80 for OCBC and $65.20 for DBS. OCBC announced that it will acquire HSBC’s International Wealth and Premier Banking business in Indonesia, which it expects to lift earnings and return on equity from the second year after completion. The report highlights that Singapore banks remain attractive due to resilient balance sheets, dividend yields and stress‑tested loan portfolios despite higher oil prices and regional currency weakness.

title: PSA Corporation Limited fined S$225,000 for 2017 worker death and files appeal
body: PSA Corporation Limited was convicted under Singapore’s Workplace Safety and Health Act for the 2017 death of employee Lee Swee Loong. The State Courts fined the company S$225,000 on June 4, which PSA paid in full by the June 12 deadline. PSA filed an appeal against both the conviction and the sentence on June 5. The court noted that a breach of the Act can carry a maximum fine of S$500,000.

title: UBS Initiates Coverage on UOB Kay Hian, Rating Buy with $4.60 Target as Stock Nears S$3.70
body: UOB Kay Hian's shares have risen to about S$3.70, nearly tripling since mid‑2024. In June 2026 UBS initiated coverage on the broker, assigning a Buy rating and a target price of $4.60 while forecasting 30% year‑on‑year commission income growth for 2026. UBS cites structural tailwinds from equity market reforms in Singapore and improving capital‑market activity in Hong Kong, but warns of medium‑term risk from fintech competitors eroding market share. Earlier, Macquarie Equity Research had initiated coverage in January 2026 with an Outperform rating, a target of S$3.12 and a 10.5× 2027 P/E multiple, highlighting liquidity benefits from Singapore reforms and growth in Malaysia.

title: Singapore Exchange to launch OTC gold clearing system by year‑end, with banks as clearing members
body: Singapore Exchange will establish an over‑the‑counter gold clearing system by the end of 2024, with interbank trading expected to build up from 2027. The Monetary Authority of Singapore will introduce gold‑vaulting services for central banks by October 2024 and remove the 5 % cap on physical precious‑metal investments under fund tax incentive schemes, with further details to be shared in September. DBS, Deutsche Bank, ICBC Standard Bank, JPMorgan, OCBC and UOB have signed a memorandum of understanding with Singapore Exchange to act as clearing members, supporting settlement of large bars and kilobars during Asian trading hours. The framework will align Singapore’s practices with LBMA Good Delivery and other global standards to deepen liquidity and improve price discovery for gold in the Asian time zone.

title: Singapore Exchange to launch OTC gold clearing system with six banks as clearing members
body: Singapore Exchange (SGX) announced it will establish an over‑the‑counter gold clearing system for Loco Singapore, with implementation targeted by the end of 2026. Six banks—DBS, Deutsche Bank, ICBC Standard Bank, JPMorgan, OCBC and UOB—will serve as clearing members of the new platform. The Monetary Authority of Singapore will introduce central‑bank gold‑vaulting services by October 2026 and will lift the 5 percent cap on physical investment precious metals under tax‑incentive schemes. SGX is also exploring a physically deliverable gold futures contract to improve price discovery and risk management during Asian trading hours.

title: Baker Technology appears undervalued with a cash‑rich balance sheet, prompting a potential privatisation offer
body: Baker Technology (BTL) is trading at S$0,495, a 0.49x price‑to‑book multiple and a 51% discount to net asset value, while its cash and short‑term deposits of S$95.2 million represent about 95% of its S$100.2 million market capitalisation. For the second half of FY2025 revenue fell 35.8% to S$25.4 million, marine offshore revenue dropped 41%, and the company swung from a S$6.1 million profit in 2H FY2024 to an S$8.0 million loss. Analyst Calvin Mau estimates that a privatisation bid would need to offer a 26.1% premium, putting the implied offer price at S$0,624 per share, which he adopts as his target price. The report notes that former CEO Dr Benety Chang, who holds about 56% of Baker Technology, could lead a buyout, and that the company’s listed subsidiary CH Offshore remains part of the group.

title: Mapletree Logistics Trust, CapitaLand Ascendas REIT and Genting Singapore Deliver 6%+ Dividend Yields
body: Mapletree Logistics Trust (MLT) reported a fourth‑quarter distribution per unit of S$0,018, a 7.0% YoY decline that masks a 0.9% operational DPU increase once one‑off divestment gains are excluded, with occupancy at 96.9% and rental reversion of +3.3% (‑2.0% in China). CapitaLand Ascendas REIT (CLAR) posted rental reversion of +10.6% across its portfolio, occupancy of 90.5%, and aggregate leverage of 42.0% that is expected to fall to about 37.3% after a S$903.5 million equity raise, while completing S$525 million of acquisitions and announcing a further S$1.1 billion pipeline including a 49% stake in a Greater Osaka data centre. Genting Singapore (G13) kept its FY2025 dividend at S$0.04 per share despite net profit dropping 32.6% YoY to S$390.3 million, free cash flow halving to S$211.3 million and capex rising 36.9% to S$578.7 million, supported by a cash balance of S$3.2 billion. The article notes that each yield is underpinned by different sources – operational cash flow for MLT, strong rental reversions and a refreshed balance sheet for CLAR, and a sizable cash war chest for Genting – highlighting varying sustainability profiles despite similar 6%+ yields.

title: Singapore Exchange to launch OTC gold clearing system as Monetary Authority of Singapore rolls out central bank gold vaulting services
body: Singapore Exchange will establish an over‑the‑counter gold clearing system for “Loco Singapore” by the end of 2026, with interbank trading slated to begin in 2027. The system will support large bars (≈12.4 kg) and kilobars (1 kg) and will involve six bullion banks—DBS Bank, Deutsche Bank, ICBC Standard Bank, JP Morgan, Oversea-Chinese Banking Corporation and United Overseas Bank—as clearing members under a memorandum of understanding signed on June 15. The Monetary Authority of Singapore will introduce central‑bank gold vaulting services for foreign central banks and sovereign entities by October 2026, extending gold accounts to selected Singapore‑based bullion banks. In parallel, DBS Bank announced tokenised physical gold for retail customers in the second half of 2026 and Oversea-Chinese Banking Corporation highlighted its tokenised gold fund and physical gold ETF as part of Singapore’s growing gold‑trading ecosystem.

title: Innotek Limited incorporates wholly‑owned subsidiary in Thailand and secures first liquid‑cooling components project
body: Innotek Limited announced the incorporation of Mansfield Technology Thailand Co Ltd, a wholly‑owned subsidiary with THB 100 million (US$3.9 million) paid‑up capital, which will begin operations in August and support a $7.5 million capital‑expenditure project to produce liquid‑cooling components, with mass production slated for October. The news lifted Innotek’s shares by 6.5 cents, or 10.2%, to 70 cents, and the new subsidiary will complement the group’s Rayong facility, which is undergoing a 15,772 sqm expansion expected to be operational in 3QFY2026.

title: Foundation Healthcare Holdings plans Singapore IPO to raise up to S$500 million
body: Foundation Healthcare Holdings intends to file its IPO prospectus in Singapore in the coming days, aiming to raise as much as S$500 million. The offering could value the company at more than US$1 billion and may be listed in the third quarter. The company is backed by SeaTown Holdings, which invested S$150 million in Foundation Healthcare in 2023, and other shareholders include Blue7, Citrine Capital, the family of Kuik Ah Han and Rizal Gozali of Jefferies Financial Group. Singapore’s IPO market this year has seen five listings raise about US$912 million, with UI Boustead Reit’s debut accounting for the bulk of that total.

title: Singapore's Straits Times Index climbs 1% on June 15 after US‑Iran peace deal
body: The Straits Times Index rose 1.3% in morning trading, peaked above 5,094 and closed up 1% at 5,077.29 on June 15 following the US‑Iran peace framework that could reopen the Strait of Hormuz. Analysts noted that transport operators ComfortDelGro and Singapore Airlines gained on lower fuel‑cost expectations, while utility players Sembcorp and Keppel also moved into the green. The Singapore Exchange (SGX) and the three local banks rose on expectations of higher trading volumes and wealth‑management demand, and property trusts Mapletree, CapitaLand, Hongkong Land and City Developments benefited from the oil price slump that pushed Brent crude down more than 4% to about US$83. Energy‑linked firms such as Seatrium fell back after earlier war‑time gains, whereas semiconductor‑linked tech manufacturers UMS, Frencken and AEM received upward re‑ratings. Overall, 25 of the 30 STI constituents traded higher, reflecting broader risk‑on sentiment spurred by the geopolitical de‑escalation.

title: How to Start Dividend Investing in Singapore While Avoiding Yield Traps
body: Dividend investing in Singapore focuses on building a portfolio of quality businesses and REITs that can deliver sustainable payouts rather than chasing the highest yields. Investors are advised to set clear income goals, select companies with stable earnings, healthy cash flow and manageable debt, and diversify across sectors and payout dates. The article cites examples such as DBS Group Holdings Ltd, which reported a 16.2% return on equity and a dividend of S$3.06 per share for FY2025, and Oversea‑Chinese Banking Corporation with a trailing yield of about 4.3% and a 60% payout ratio, as well as REITs like CapitaLand Integrated Commercial Trust (8.0% year‑on‑year revenue growth) and Parkway Life REIT (≈3.8% trailing yield). It also highlights the importance of monitoring gearing, occupancy and interest‑cost pressures for REITs and using dividend reinvestment to compound returns over time.

title: Foundation Healthcare Holdings plans to file IPO prospectus in Singapore
body: Foundation Healthcare Holdings Pte Ltd intends to file its IPO prospectus in Singapore in the coming days. The offering aims to raise up to $500 million, which could value the company at more than $1 billion (about $1.28 billion). The company is backed by SeaTown Holdings Pte Ltd, which invested $150 million in 2023, and other shareholders include Blue7 Pte Ltd, Citrine Capital Sdn Bhd, the family of property tycoon Kuik Ah Han and Rizal Gozali of Jefferies Financial Group Inc. Singapore’s IPO market has raised roughly $912 million from five listings this year, with UI Boustead Real Estate Investment Trust accounting for the majority of that total.

title: Foundation Healthcare plans Singapore IPO targeting up to S$500 million raise
body: Foundation Healthcare Holdings intends to file its IPO prospectus in Singapore in the coming days, aiming to raise as much as S$500 million. The offering could value the company at more than US$1 billion and may be priced for a listing in the third quarter. The IPO is backed by SeaTown Holdings, which invested S$150 million in Foundation Healthcare in 2023. Singapore’s IPO market has raised about US$912 million from five listings this year, with UI Boustead Reit accounting for the bulk of that total.

title: PUB allocates S$12 million to develop water‑efficiency solutions for wafer fabrication and data centres
body: Singapore's national water agency PUB will channel S$12 million (US$9.36 million) to develop cost‑effective water‑treatment and recycling solutions for wafer‑fabrication plants and to improve water efficiency in data centres, Deputy Prime Minister Gan Kim Yong announced on 16 June. The funding is part of a total S$97 million allocation from the National Research Foundation under the RIE 2030 urban solutions and sustainability domain, with S$85 million earmarked for municipal water innovations and S$12 million dedicated to the two target sectors. PUB will form Industrial Water Solutions Innovation Ecosystem Alliances, partnering with the START centre, Singapore Water Association and Singapore Semiconductor Industry Association for wafer fabrication, and with the Sustainable Tropical Data Centre Testbed, SWA and SGTech for data centres. The initiative follows recent expansion announcements by Micron Technology and Applied Materials in Singapore, which are cited as catalysts but not the focus of the funding.

title: Elite UK REIT to acquire five government‑leased properties for £31.9 million and launch £19.0 million conversion of Lindsay House
body: Elite UK REIT announced that its wholly‑owned subsidiary Elite Kist Limited has signed conditional share and asset purchase agreements to buy five freehold or virtual freehold UK properties for £31.9 million. The properties are expected to generate about £2.6 million of gross rental income annually and, on a pro‑forma basis, will lift the REIT’s FY2025 distribution per unit (DPU) by 1.3% to 3,051 pence and raise the portfolio valuation roughly 7% to £492.1 million. The REIT also plans a £19.0 million capital expenditure to convert Lindsay House into a 170‑bed purpose‑built student accommodation, with funding coming from existing debt borrowings of £30.7 million, a new unit issuance of up to £8.9 million to Elite UK Commercial Fund III, and a £7.4 million private placement. Units in Elite UK REIT were last traded at £0.34 on June 15 after a trading halt was announced.

title: Binance prepares for possible EU exit as Greek licence remains pending
body: Binance Holdings Ltd is preparing to stop providing services in the European Union because it has not yet received a licence from Greece’s Hellenic Capital Market Commission. Under the EU Markets in Crypto‑assets (MiCA) regime, crypto firms must obtain a licence in at least one member state by July or they must wind down operations in the bloc. Binance said it will notify EU customers as early as Tuesday and is focused on minimising any disruption for users while the licence decision is pending.

title: Five Singapore Companies That Pass the ‘Wallet Test’ with Strong Earnings and Dividends
body: The article’s “Wallet Test” highlights five Singapore‑based firms that generate steady cash flow and dividends: Sheng Siong Group Ltd, DBS Group Holdings Ltd, Singapore Telecommunications Limited, ComfortDelGro Corporation Limited and CapitaLand Integrated Commercial Trust. Sheng Siong reported Q1 2026 revenue of S$452.8 million (up 12.4% YoY) and net profit of S$43.4 million, while DBS posted a 17.0% ROE, an ordinary dividend of S$0.66 plus a S$0.15 capital‑return dividend, and net profit of S$2.93 billion, a 1% YoY increase. Singapore Telecommunications Limited’s FY2026 underlying net profit rose 12% to S$2.77 billion and it declared a record annual dividend of S$0,185 per share; ComfortDelGro Corporation Limited’s FY2025 revenue reached S$5.06 billion (up 13%) with profit of S$230.3 million and a dividend increase to S$0,0850 per share; CapitaLand Integrated Commercial Trust’s Q1 2026 net property income grew 7.9% to S$314.4 million, with occupancy at 95.2% and leverage at 38.5%. The piece notes that despite competitive pressures and macro‑economic headwinds, each company’s strong earnings, cash balances and dividend policies make them attractive for long‑term investors.

title: Three Singapore REITs Seen as Strong Long-Term Holds
body: CapitaLand Integrated Commercial Trust (CICT) reported 95.2% occupancy and a three‑year weighted average lease expiry as of 31 March 2026, with rental reversions of 4.4% for retail and 6.1% for office and a DPU increase from S$0,1075 in 2023 to S$0,1158 in 2025. Frasers Centrepoint Trust (FCT) posted 99.8% occupancy, 6.5% rental reversions in the first half of FY2026, and a DPU rise from S$0,1001 in 2012 to S$0,1211 in 2025, backed by sponsor Frasers Property. Parkway Life REIT, which owns 74 healthcare properties across Singapore, Japan and France, showed a 14.85‑year WALE, gearing of 34.2%, interest coverage of 8.4 times and a DPU growth from S$0,1075 in 2013 to S$0,1529 in 2025, with tenants such as Parkway Hospitals Singapore, a wholly owned subsidiary of IHH Healthcare. The article argues that the combination of high‑quality assets, strong sponsor support and prudent capital management makes these REITs suitable for buy‑and‑hold portfolios.

title: iX Biopharma moves manufacturing equipment to Nevada to fulfill $41 million US Department of Defense contract
body: iX Biopharma announced it will relocate its manufacturing machinery from Australia to its JV partner Orion Specialty Labs’ facility in Nevada, targeting completion in the third quarter of 2026. The relocation is driven by a sole‑source US$41 million contract from the US Department of Defense to develop the Wafermine sublingual ketamine wafer and to meet the Buy American Act requirements for an Emergency Use Authorisation. Since the Pentagon award, iX’s share price has risen to 38 cents, a 2,100 % gain over the past year, and Phillip Securities issued a “buy” recommendation in April 2026 with a target price of $1.00, implying roughly a 5 × upside from the 20‑cent level. The company is also restructuring its consumer business for a possible spin‑off listing on the SGX or Nasdaq, positioning its US infrastructure as a potential acquisition target for larger pharma groups.

title: Credit Bureau Asia, Micro-Mechanics and Kimly Conduct Small-Scale Share Buybacks
body: Credit Bureau Asia (SGX: TCU) repurchased S$113,170 of its shares in the first five months of 2026, supported by S$71.1 million of liquid assets and free cash flow of S$27.2 million, allowing it to raise its full‑year dividend to S$0,042 per share. Micro‑Mechanics (Holdings) Ltd (SGX: 590) bought back S$368,321 of stock while reporting Q3 FY2026 revenue of S$18.6 million, net profit of S$3.8 million and ending the quarter with S$25.7 million cash and no borrowings, though free cash flow fell to S$2.8 million. Kimly (SGX: 1D0) repurchased S$538,682 of shares, posted half‑year revenue of S$161.4 million and profit of S$16.4 million, held S$65.1 million cash against S$10.6 million borrowings and kept its interim dividend at S$0,010 per share.

title: MOM seeks higher fine for PSA over 2017 Keppel Terminal worker death
body: The Ministry of Manpower has lodged an appeal seeking a higher penalty for PSA Corporation Limited over the 2017 death of a worker at Keppel Terminal. PSA was convicted of a Workplace Safety and Health Act offence on 16 March and fined S$225,000 on 4 June, which it paid by the 12 June deadline. The appeal asks for an increased fine in the range of S$300,000 to S$350,000, citing systemic safety failures spanning more than a decade. PSA had previously filed an appeal against the conviction and sentence on 5 June.

title: Jardine Matheson Holdings sets $5.1 billion portfolio recycling target through 2030
body: Jardine Matheson Holdings announced at its first Investor Day that it aims to recycle at least $5.1 billion (US$4 billion) from its portfolio by 2030, excluding commitments from Hongkong Land and Astra. The group also targets generating at least $256.3 million (US$200 million) of additional profit from new acquisitions over the same period and will run a $640.9 million (US$500 million) share‑buyback programme through the end of 2027. It set a goal of at least 9% annualised five‑year total shareholder return and a minimum 5% yearly dividend growth, while seeking control or joint‑control positions in cash‑generative, technology‑enabled businesses that can deliver more than $128.2 million (US$100 million) profit after tax within five years. The targets follow JMH’s recent $3.1 billion investment to acquire a 100% stake in I‑MED Radiology Network.

title: DBS Group and Singapore Exchange boost dividends, delivering S$0.81 and S$0.1125 per share respectively
body: DBS Group paid a total dividend of S$0.81 per share in May 2024, comprising S$0.66 ordinary dividend and a S$0.15 capital return. Singapore Exchange paid S$0,1125 per share in the same month. Both companies have increased their payouts over the past five years, with DBS rising from S$0.16 per share in 2020 to S$0.66 ordinary dividend in 2024, and SGX growing from about S$0.08 per share five years ago to the current level, with a pledge to add a quarter‑cent every three months through 2028. The higher payouts helped a Smart Dividend Portfolio generate nearly S$3,000 in dividend income this year.

title: Keppel FELS (now Seatrium New Energy) manager acquitted of alleged S$300,000 kickback scheme
body: A Singapore district court on June 17 cleared Alvin Lim Wee Lun, former shipyard manager of Keppel FELS, of all 46 charges alleging he received nearly S$300,000 in kickbacks. Keppel FELS, now part of Seatrium and operating as Seatrium New Energy, was the shipyard where the alleged scheme took place. Prosecutors had calculated a 15 % cut of marked‑up invoices amounting to S$294,208.98, while the defence argued Lim only received about S$4,000. The acquittal was based on inconsistencies in the testimony of former assistant manager Rajavikraman Jayapandian, who had a possible motive to implicate Lim.

title: Accrelist Ltd appoints new CEO and outlines 51% China aesthetics acquisition
body: Accrelist Ltd has appointed Derek Cheong Sheng Ze as CEO effective 16 June, according to an SGXNet filing. The group entered a non‑binding term sheet to acquire a 51% stake in a newly incorporated Chinese target that will operate aesthetic businesses, with the A.M Aesthetics brand licensed royalty‑free for early market deployment. Accrelist said the transaction includes performance‑linked valuation terms and will give visibility on the underlying business before completion. The company also indicated it will review its broader portfolio, including its 52.5% stake in Jubilee Industries Holdings Ltd and its 27.34% stake in MClean Technologies Berhad, as part of ongoing capital allocation considerations.

title: Three Singapore dividend stocks offer solid yields and earnings growth
body: OCBC Ltd reported 1Q2026 net profit of S$1.97 billion, a 5% YoY rise, and declared a total FY2025 dividend of S$0.99 per share, giving a trailing yield of about 4.1% based on its S$24.26 share price. Frasers Centrepoint Trust posted 1HFY2026 gross revenue of S$221.9 million and net property income of S$160.8 million, raising its distribution per unit to S$0,06136 and delivering an annualised yield of roughly 5.4% from a unit price of S$2.27. Singapore Exchange Limited posted a record adjusted net profit of S$357.1 million for 1HFY2026, increased its interim quarterly dividend to S$0.11 per share (annualised yield about 2% on a S$24.17 price) and expects quarterly dividends to grow by S$0,0025 annually through FY2028. Together, the three stocks illustrate how a diversified portfolio of a bank, a REIT and an exchange can help investors target a S$500 passive‑income goal.

title: Centurion Corp acquires 25% stake in Perth student accommodation for A$250,000
body: Centurion Corp, through its wholly‑owned subsidiary Centurion Overseas Investments (II) Pte. Ltd, acquired a 25% equity interest in a 182‑bed purpose‑built student accommodation at 55‑57 Fairway, Crawley, Perth for A$250,000 ($225,475). The remaining 75% is held by Centurion Properties Australia Investments Pty. Ltd, a wholly‑owned subsidiary of Centurion Corp’s controlling shareholder, which is itself a subsidiary of Centurion Properties and ultimately of Centurion Global Ltd, the equal owners of Centurion Corp. The property, to be managed under Centurion Corp’s Epiisod student accommodation brand, is expected to be completed in 2Q2027. Centurion Corp’s shares closed 2 cents higher, up 1.34% at $1.51 on June 17.

title: US firms sue Singamas, China International Marine Containers and CXIC Group Containers over alleged container price-fixing
body: US manufacturers Singamas, China International Marine Containers and CXIC Group Containers, along with their executives including CEO and chairman Teo Siong Seng of Singamas, have been sued in separate class‑action lawsuits by CA Spalding Company and Daybreak Express. The suits, filed on June 2 and June 9, allege the companies conspired to restrict output and fix prices of standard dry shipping containers, which account for roughly 95 % of global supply. According to the filings, the alleged scheme caused container prices to roughly double between 2019 and 2021 and boosted the manufacturers’ profits by about one hundred times. The plaintiffs are seeking multiple or treble monetary damages for the overcharges they incurred.

title: CSE Global faces 1H margin pressure but retains BUY rating with target S$1.79
body: CSE Global’s share price fell from a peak of about $1.80 in late May 2026 to around $1.40 after management warned that start‑up costs for its new U.S. electrification facility will compress 1H2026 margins. Despite the governance dispute involving the resignation of lead independent director Tan Chian Khong, the company reported 1Q26 revenue up 29% YoY to S$265 million, order intake up 75% YoY to S$271 million and a robust orderbook of S$716 million. UOB KH maintains a BUY recommendation with an unchanged target price of S$1.79, implying about 30% upside from the current S$1.37 level and a 29× 2027 forward PE multiple. The analysts expect the margin pressure to ease in 2H26 as the new facility reaches steady‑state production and the orderbook converts to revenue, while noting that Heliconia remains a major shareholder of CSE Global.

title: AEM Holdings reports 35.8% revenue jump as AI demand boosts SGX tech stocks
body: AEM Holdings (SGX: AWX) saw Q1 2026 revenue climb 35.8% YoY to S$116.9 million and net profit surge 329.4% to S$14.3 million, with its Test Cell Solutions segment contributing S$88.1 million (about 75% of revenue) and FY2026 revenue guidance lifted to S$550‑600 million. UMS Integration (SGX: 558) posted Q1 revenue of S$69.4 million up 20% YoY, semiconductor segment revenue of S$58.9 million, net profit of S$14.0 million, but its free cash flow turned negative to –S$8.9 million and gross margin slipped to 53%. Venture Corporation (SGX: V03) recorded modest Q1 revenue growth of 1.9% YoY to S$628.5 million, net profit S$56.3 million at a 9.0% margin, and AI‑related Portfolio B sales added S$42 million while Portfolio A fell by S$30 million. All three firms remain cash‑rich, with AEM holding net cash of S$56.5 million, UMS cash of S$34.3 million against S$8.3 million debt, and Venture maintaining over S$1 billion in net cash, underscoring strong balance sheets amid AI‑driven growth.

title: Parkway Life REIT, CapitaLand Integrated Commercial Trust, and CapitaLand Ascendas REIT Highlight Different Dividend Drivers in Latest Results
body: Parkway Life REIT reported FY2026 gross revenue of S$38.2 million, down 2.1% YoY, with net property income of S$35.8 million, yet its distribution per unit rose 15.1% YoY to S$0,044, driven by higher Singapore hospital rent after a rent rebate ended. CapitaLand Integrated Commercial Trust posted an 8.0% YoY increase in gross revenue to S$426.7 million and a 7.9% rise in net property income to S$314.4 million, supported by full ownership of CapitaSpring, higher shopper traffic and tenant sales, and rental reversions of +4.4% for retail and +6.1% for office. The trust also proposed a S$3.9 billion acquisition of Paragon, funded partly by the planned S$2.48 billion sale of Asia Square Tower 2, and expects a pro‑forma DPU accretion of 1.7%. CapitaLand Ascendas REIT recorded rental reversion of +10.6% (US +15.1%, Singapore +10.5%), closed S$525 million of acquisitions and announced a S$1.1 billion investment including a 49% stake in an Osaka hyperscale data centre, while aggregate leverage stood at 42.0% and is projected to fall to about 37.3% after a S$903.5 million equity raise.

title: iFAST and DBS highlighted as ideal graduation‑gift stocks after strong Q1 2026 earnings
body: iFAST Corporation Ltd., a wealth‑management fintech with a global digital platform, reported Q1 2026 revenue of S$154.5 million, up 44.5% YoY, and net profit of S$28.0 million, up 47.3% YoY. Its assets under administration rose 27.1% YoY to a record S$32.6 billion, supported by net inflows of S$1.25 billion, and it held cash and cash equivalents of S$620.0 million against debt of S$235.7 million, leaving net cash of S$384.4 million. DBS Group Holdings Ltd., Singapore’s largest bank by assets, posted record total income of S$5.95 billion in Q1 2026, a 1% YoY increase despite rate headwinds. The board declared a dividend of S$0.81 per share (ordinary S$0.66 plus capital return S$0.15), an 8% rise from the prior year’s S$0.75. The author suggests both stocks as long‑term graduation gifts to teach children about ownership and compounding returns.

title: Centurion acquires 25% stake in Perth student housing project, expanding its PBSA pipeline
body: Centurion has acquired a 25% equity interest in a 182‑bed purpose‑built student accommodation (PBSA) project near the University of Western Australia for AUD 250,000 cash, marking its latest capital‑light expansion in Australia. The deal follows the September 2025 spin‑off of its accommodation assets into the Centurion Accommodation REIT (CAREIT), which reduced Centurion’s net debt‑to‑equity ratio from 29% in FY24 to 12% and crystallised roughly SGD 1.8 billion of assets. DBS Research notes the acquisition is strategic rather than earnings‑accretive, adding to a pipeline that aims to deliver about 2,198 new beds between 2027‑2028 and over 4,000 beds through FY2027, while Centurion retains a 38.1% stake in CAREIT and a target price of SGD 1.86. Management says the Perth project strengthens its PBSA presence and could later be injected into CAREIT, supporting long‑term shareholder value with minimal balance‑sheet risk.

title: Sunway MCL and CSC Land Group top River Valley tender with $750.6 million bid
body: Sunway MCL and CSC Land Group, through their joint venture, submitted the winning bid of $750.6 million for the River Valley Green (Parcel C) residential site under the Government Land Sales programme. The bid translates to $1,730 per square foot per plot ratio for a 500‑unit, two‑tower development of more than 500 units adjacent to Great World MRT Station in District 9.

title: SDAI Limited secures up to $600,000 loan facility
body: SDAI Limited entered into a funding agreement with private investor Tan Kooi Jin for a loan facility of up to $600,000, signed on 17 June 2026. Each drawdown may not exceed $300,000 and must be repaid within six calendar months with simple interest of 15% per annum calculated daily. The proceeds will be used solely for prepayment or payment of AKG products to support the commercialization of longevity and anti‑ageing products. Tan, who holds 814,700 shares (0.19%) of SDAI and an indirect minority stake in OOWAY Technology Pte. Ltd., is an existing shareholder, and SDAI’s shares have been suspended from trading on the Singapore Exchange since 12 July 2021.

title: AI demand lifts earnings and cash flow at Micro-Mechanics, Nanofilm and Valuetronics
body: Micro-Mechanics (Holdings) Ltd reported Q3FY2026 revenue of S$18.6 million, up 16.2% YoY, with net profit of S$3.8 million and a gross margin expansion to 51.6% driven by a 20.9% jump in consumable tools sales linked to AI, computing and memory demand. Nanofilm Technologies International Limited posted Q1 2026 revenue of S$55 million, a 24% YoY rise, with its Advanced Materials unit contributing S$49 million and margins improving sharply to a 39% gross profit margin and 26% EBITDA margin. Valuetronics Holdings Limited saw FY2026 revenue decline 4.0% to HK$1.66 billion and net profit fall 33.1% to HK$111.4 million, but free cash flow turned positive to HK$178.4 million, cash rose to HK$1.21 billion and the dividend increased 41% to HK$0.38 per share. The three SGX‑listed firms illustrate how AI‑driven demand is translating into higher revenues, margin recovery and stronger cash generation across the semiconductor supply chain.

title: Chasen Holdings Posts S$7.2 million Profit and 68% YTD Stock Gain
body: Chasen Holdings swung from an S$11.8 million loss in FY2025 to a S$7.2 million net profit in FY2026, helped by a S$6.8 million fair‑value gain and an expanded gross margin of 19.7%. The company’s small‑cap shares, trading at 14.6 cents, have risen 68% year‑to‑date as it pursues specialist relocation projects, recently securing a US$18 million contract with a Japanese EV‑battery customer and targeting at least 20% revenue growth backed by S$45 million of FY2027 projects. Management highlighted a 70% occupancy at the newly built Chasen Logistics Hub, a revalued amount of S$110 million, and a 60% market share in China’s TFT LCD relocation market, while planning workforce expansion in India and the US.

title: Three SGX REITs to distribute dividends in the week of 22 June 2026
body: Frasers Logistics & Commercial Trust will pay on 22 June, reporting first‑half FY2026 gross revenue of S$238.9 million (up 2.8% YoY), adjusted net property income of S$167.0 million (up 3.6%) and operational DPU of S$0,02820 (up 11.9% YoY) despite headline DPU slipping 1.7% to S$0,02950. Mapletree Logistics Trust will pay on 23 June; for Q4 FY2025/26 it posted gross revenue of S$176.6 million (down 1.7% YoY), NPI of S$151.4 million (down 0.9%) and operational DPU rising 0.9% YoY to S$0,0189, with occupancy at 96.9% and rental reversion improving to +3.3%. First REIT will pay on 26 June, with Q1 2026 rental and other income down 8.4% to S$23.2 million, DPU falling 13.8% to S$0,00500, occupancy at 100%, and a planned divestiture of eight Indonesian hospitals and three non‑core assets for S$471.5 million while gearing stands at 44.6% and debt cost improves to 3.9%. The analysis highlights that operational DPU grew for FLCT and MLT despite headline declines, whereas First REIT’s distribution pressure is driven by currency effects and a deliberate portfolio overhaul rather than asset weakness.

title: FJ Benjamin Holdings raises $302,400 via private placement to Rosslyn Leong and Richard Eu
body: Retailer FJ Benjamin Holdings announced a private placement of 42 million new shares at 0.72 cents each, raising $302,400, which represents a 10% discount to the VWAP of 0.8 cents. The placement is subscribed by medical doctor Rosslyn Leong Sou Fong for 28 million shares and Richard Eu Yee Ming for 14 million shares, giving them post‑placement holdings of 2.28% and 1.14% of the company respectively. FJ Benjamin describes the investors as third‑party private investors with no prior shareholdings or business dealings with the company, and says the raise is part of its capital‑management strategy to strengthen its financial position. The retailer reported widening losses, with a 1HFY2026 loss of $9.52 million versus $4.36 million a year earlier and a negative working capital of $1.9 million as of 31 Dec 2025.

title: Holding Cash While Monitoring Microsoft and Sheng Siong
body: The author explains a strategy of maintaining cash to stay flexible amid market uncertainty. Microsoft reported FY2025 revenue of $281.7 billion, up 15%, net income of $101.8 billion (+16%) and operating cash flow of $136.2 billion, with cloud revenue reaching $168.9 billion, a 23% increase. Sheng Siong Group posted 1Q2026 revenue of S$452.8 million (+12.4% YoY) and net profit of S$43.4 million (+12.6%), ending the quarter with S$461.1 million cash and zero debt while operating 87 stores. The author views both firms as quality businesses worth holding for the long term while waiting for more attractive entry points.

title: How to Combine ETFs and Singapore Stocks for a Balanced Portfolio
body: Investors can build a balanced portfolio by anchoring the core with diversified ETFs and adding Singapore blue‑chip stocks as satellites. DBS Group reported a 4.2% dividend yield and declared a S$0.81 dividend for 1Q2026, comprising S$0.66 ordinary and S$0.15 capital return, giving an annualised total of S$3.24. OCBC offered a 4% dividend yield, reinforcing its role as a stable income source. Singapore Technologies Engineering posted S$3.3 billion revenue in 1Q2026, an 11% YoY increase, and paid a total dividend of S$0.23 for FY2025 with an interim S$0.04 in 1Q2026. CapitaLand Integrated Commercial Trust delivered a distribution per unit of S$0,1158 for FY2025, up 6.4% from the prior year.

title: BlackGold Natural Resources Limited to transfer 85% control to PT Rajawali Artha Global in $1.6m restructuring
body: BlackGold Natural Resources Limited, currently under judicial management, agreed to hand an 85% controlling stake to PT Rajawali Artha Global as part of a restructuring tied to a $1.6 million investment funding agreement. The scheme, approved by creditors on 31 December 2025, proposes a 38‑cent‑on‑the‑dollar recovery for admitted claims while RAG will subscribe for new shares and fund scheme costs, including a $90,000 initial payment and up to $400,000 for professional fees. After completion, RAG will own 85% of BlackGold’s enlarged share capital, diluting existing shareholders to 15%, and the transaction may trigger mandatory general offer obligations under the Singapore Code on Take‑overs and Mergers. Completion remains subject to creditor approval, court sanction, shareholder and regulatory clearances, and an eight‑month extension of judicial management sought until 23 March 2027.

title: Foundation Healthcare Holdings files draft prospectus for Singapore Exchange listing
body: Foundation Healthcare Holdings, an integrated private healthcare platform in Singapore, has lodged its draft prospectus to list on the Singapore Exchange. The company posted a loss of $7.66 million in FY2023 but recorded earnings of $10.12 million in FY2024 and $14 million in FY2025, with total comprehensive income rising to $41.2 million in FY2025 and revenue increasing from $112.4 million in FY2023 to $231.2 million in FY2025. Ownership is 88.6% indirect holding by Temasek, with Kuik Pte Ltd (1.3%) and KCM Investments (1%) as minority shareholders, and cornerstone investors include Amova Asset Management Asia, Aregence Capital Management, Granite Asia Capital, Hood River Capital Management, Lion Global Investors, Manulife Investment Management (Singapore), Orbit Master Holdings, RBC Global Asset Management (Asia), UBS and World Bank-linked International Finance Corporation. Proceeds will fund acquisitions of clinical practices and medical centres and support regional expansion, and the company will not pay dividends in FY2026 and FY2027 to reinvest earnings.

title: Keppel DC REIT records 13% DPU increase as CICT and CLAR defer payouts
body: Keppel DC REIT reported distributable income of S$74.6 million, a 20.7% YoY rise, and its distribution per unit climbed 13.2% to S$0,02833, supported by gross revenue of S$121.0 million and aggregate leverage falling to 35.1% with roughly S$550 million debt headroom. CapitaLand Integrated Commercial Trust posted S$426.7 million gross revenue (up 8.0% YoY) and net property income of S$314.4 million, with rental reversions of +4.4% retail and +6.1% office, while it proposed a S$3.9 billion acquisition of Paragon funded by a S$2.48 billion divestment of Asia Square Tower 2, implying a prospective 1.7% pro‑forma DPU accretion. CapitaLand Ascendas REIT saw portfolio rental reversion of +10.6% (US leases +15.1%) and added a fully‑occupied Spanish logistics portfolio, but occupancy slipped to 90.5% and aggregate leverage rose to 42.0% before a S$903.5 million equity raise expected to bring leverage back to about 37.3%. The analysis cautions investors to assess whether each REIT’s payouts are funded by operating cash rather than financial engineering, noting that only Keppel DC REIT delivered actual DPU growth this quarter while the other two await half‑year results.

title: Hidden‑gem dividend stocks on the SGX show cash‑backed payouts
body: HRnetGroup reported FY2025 revenue of S$584.0 million, profit of S$51.2 million and generated free cash flow of S$52.0 million, supporting a raised dividend of S$0,042 per share with no debt. VICOM, a subsidiary of ComfortDelGro Corporation Ltd, posted Q1 2026 revenue of S$37.2 million, operating profit of S$12.0 million and net profit of S$10.0 million, but free cash flow fell to S$2.2 million as it invested S$11.6 million in a new testing centre and did not declare a dividend for the quarter. Elite UK REIT held a portfolio valued at £460.2 million, saw Q1 2026 revenue of £9.4 million and adjusted net property income rise of 4.0%, with distributable income of £5.3 million, occupancy of 99.9% and net gearing reduced to 37.4%. The article highlights that each company’s dividend sustainability stems from strong cash generation, low leverage and stable tenant or client bases, making them attractive for retirement income.

title: Singtel gains $140 million from partial sale of Gulf Development stake
body: Singtel Group sold 2.8% of its stake in Gulf Development for about $1 billion, generating cumulative equity gains of roughly $140 million. After the transaction Singtel retains a 4.95% holding in Gulf Development valued at about $1.8 billion. The divestment adds to Singtel’s capital‑recycling programme, which has unlocked $6.8 billion toward its $9 billion mid‑term target and supports its ongoing $2 billion value‑realisation share buyback, of which 34% has been deployed at a cost of $681 million. Singtel’s FY2026 dividend proposal includes a core dividend of 13.4 cents per share and a value‑realisation dividend of 5.1 cents, totalling 18.5 cents, while its shares traded at $4.35, down 0.23%.

title: ComfortDelGro launches driverless shuttles in Singapore's Punggol
body: ComfortDelGro, a transport operator, began public rides on its Zig Driverless shuttles in Punggol on 22 June. The launch is the company's second autonomous service globally after a robotaxi pilot in Guangzhou, China. ComfortDelGro said its China and Singapore operations will support a wider rollout as it aims to convert about 10% of its global point‑to‑point fleet to autonomous vehicles by 2030. The service is offered free of charge with pick‑up and drop‑off points at Sam Kee, Northshore and Punggol Coast Mall.

title: CSE Global faces board governance dispute after lead independent director resigns
body: On June 2, lead independent director Tan Chian Khong resigned from CSE Global, citing unresolved differences with controlling shareholder Heliconia Capital Management. CSE disclosed that chairman Eugene Lai, who is Heliconia’s board nominee, allegedly asked Tan to step down and to relinquish his role as chair of the nominating committee, which Lai denied. Singapore Exchange Regulation (SGX Regco) prompted CSE to provide additional details, highlighting the regulator’s “buyer beware” stance and the need for greater transparency on material matters. The dispute underscores governance risks for CSE as it undergoes a strategic review by Jefferies, and shareholders are urged to ensure independent directors can operate without undue influence from Heliconia.

title: Sheng Siong Group Ltd Insider Lim Hock Leng to by way of gift Reports Shareholding Change
body: Lim Hock Leng, an insider of Sheng Siong Group Ltd, reported a change in shareholding. The transaction involved a gift of 2,666,666 shares, reducing his direct interest from 799,098,459 to 776,431,793 shares. His stake decreased from 53.15% to 51.64%.

title: Sheng Siong Group Ltd Transfer from Lim Hock Chee to Daughter
body: Lim Hock Chee transferred 20,000,000 shares of Sheng Siong Group Ltd to his daughter as a gift, reducing his ownership from 52.62% to 51.12%.

title: DBS Group Holdings posts record fee income and an 8% dividend increase as part of a 12‑month Singapore dividend portfolio
body: DBS Group Holdings delivered record total income of S$5.95 billion in 1Q2026, with net profit of S$2.93 billion (up 1% YoY) and an 8% dividend increase to S$0.81 per share (S$0.66 ordinary plus S$0.15 capital return). Mapletree Logistics Trust’s 4QFY2025/2026 distribution per unit fell 7% to S$0,018, but operational DPU rose 0.9% YoY, occupancy improved to 96.9% and it recycled assets by divesting six properties at roughly a 20% premium and acquiring a logistics park in Mumbai for S$53.2 million. Singapore Exchange reported 1HFY2026 net revenue of S$695.4 million (up 7.6% YoY) and adjusted net profit of S$357.1 million (up 11.6% YoY), while committing to a quarterly dividend increase of 0.25 cents through FY2028. The quarterly payout schedules of DBS (April, May, August, November), Mapletree Logistics Trust (March, June, September, December) and Singapore Exchange (February, May, October, November) together cover ten of the twelve months, leaving January and July to be filled by the Phillip SGX APAC Dividend Leaders REIT ETF.

title: Vicom CEO Sim Wing Yew to retire, deputy Chung Tying Chun named successor
body: Vicom announced that CEO Sim Wing Yew will retire on Dec 31 after 14 years, and deputy CEO Chung Tying Chun will assume the CEO role on Jan 1, 2027. Chung, who previously led Vicom subsidiary Setsco Services, will step down as Setsco’s CEO on July 1, with Ng Soon Lee becoming acting CEO. The transition is part of Vicom’s succession planning to ensure continuity and drive growth in the testing, inspection and certification sector. Vicom shares closed 1 cent higher, up 0.56% at $1.79 on June 24.

title: SMCL Haven 3 Pte. Ltd and CSC Land Group (Singapore) Pte. Ltd win River Valley Green Parcel C tender with $750.6 million bid
body: SMCL Haven 3 Pte. Ltd and CSC Land Group (Singapore) Pte. Ltd, forming a consortium, were awarded the River Valley Green Parcel C site by the Urban Redevelopment Authority. The consortium submitted the highest bid of $750.6 million, equivalent to $1,730 per square foot of plot ratio. The 11,516‑square‑metre parcel permits up to 40,306 square metres of gross floor area for residential development under a 99‑year lease. The tender was launched on 9 April and closed on 18 June.

title: OUE REIT proposes $500 million divestment of Crowne Plaza Changi Airport and $20 million special distribution
body: OUE REIT (SGX:TS0U) announced a proposal to sell the Crowne Plaza Changi Airport hotel for $500 million, representing a 1.3% premium to independent valuations. After a $1.5 million divestment cost, net cash proceeds of about $498.5 million are expected, of which $20 million will be paid to unitholders as special distributions over the first two years. The special distribution would raise the FY2025 pro‑forma distribution per unit by 5.8% to a yield of 6.6%, and using the proceeds to repay debt would lower aggregate leverage from 41.5% to 36.6%. Upon completion, roughly 94.3% of OUE REIT’s assets will be located in Singapore, and the REIT’s units were trading flat at 35.5 cents at 9:20 am.

title: Frasers Property proposes $2.1 bn FHT portfolio optimisation to boost EPS, ROE and reduce gearing
body: Frasers Property (FPL) announced a proposed optimisation of the Fraser Hospitality Trust (FHT) portfolio involving about $2.1 billion of assets. The plan, executed with co‑owner TCC Group Investments, will remove legacy rental and guarantee obligations, align property and operating company ownership and give FPL full ownership of Fraser Suites Singapore. Pro‑forma FY2025 figures show EPS rising 3.4%, ROE improving 0.1 percentage points, NAV per share up 1.3% and net gearing falling 3.3 percentage points, with the transaction priced at a 6.7% premium to the latest independent valuation. After completion, FPL’s on‑balance‑sheet hospitality assets will fall from roughly $3.7 bn to $2.5 bn while total assets under management stay at $4.2 bn, freeing capital for higher‑return opportunities.

title: Parkson Retail Asia trades at ~4× PE on >S$20 M profit and 16.7% dividend yield
body: Parkson Retail Asia, a Malaysian department‑store chain listed on SGX and part of the Lion Group empire, has seen its share price recover to 12 cents after falling to about 1 cent in 2022. The company generated more than S$20 million of net profit annually over the past three years, resulting in a price‑earnings multiple of roughly 4. Cash balances grew from S$62 million at end‑2025 to S$169 million in 1Q 2026, while trade and other payables rose to S$131.2 million, and the firm paid a special interim dividend of 4 cents per share in June 2025 and 2 cents in June 2026, yielding about 16.7% trailing. With 39 stores remaining in Malaysia after exiting Vietnam, Indonesia and Myanmar and minimal borrowings, the stock is presented as a low‑valuation, dividend‑focused play despite the risk of erratic payouts.

title: Frasers Property to sell 63.28% stake in five hotels to Thailand's TCC Group Investments
body: Frasers Property announced a restructuring of its hospitality portfolio that involves selling its 63.28% stake in five stabilised hotel assets to TCC Group Investments Limited (TCCGI). The five hotels, valued at S$1.1 billion, will be jointly owned after the deal, with Frasers Property retaining an effective 49.95% exposure and TCCGI holding 50.05%. The transaction, part of a broader portfolio optimisation that also categorises four potential‑yield assets (S$0.4 billion) and four non‑core assets (S$0.3 billion) for future divestment, is expected to free capital for higher‑return opportunities and enhance shareholder value. TCCGI, already a 36.72% stakeholder in Frasers Hospitality Trust and the largest shareholder of Frasers Property Limited, will become the primary co‑owner of the sold assets.

title: MSCI to acquire climate‑risk data firm First Street for $120 million
body: MSCI announced it will acquire First Street, a provider of physics‑based climate‑risk data and analytics, for US$120 million in cash. The transaction, expected to close in Q3 2026 with possible earn‑out payments over the next two years, will move First Street’s results into MSCI’s sustainability and climate segment and integrate its property‑level data into MSCI’s climate and geospatial solutions.

title: Three SGX small‑caps set June 2026 dividend payouts
body: LHN Limited will pay an interim dividend of S$0.01 per share on 26 June 2026 after reporting 1HFY2026 revenue of S$60.9 million (‑13.7% YoY), net profit of S$16.8 million (+18.6%) and free cash flow of S$22.7 million. Straits Trading Company will pay an interim dividend of S$0.08 per share on 29 June 2026 despite a FY2025 loss of S$249.1 million, supported by free cash flow of S$27.6 million, cash of S$488.4 million and reduced borrowings to S$1.4 billion. Yeo Hiap Seng will pay a final dividend of S$0.02 per share on 29 June 2026 after FY2025 revenue fell 11% to S$292.4 million, net profit rose to S$21.1 million driven by a S$40.9 million fair‑value gain, while free cash flow turned negative to S$‑7.4 million. The three companies, respectively a real‑estate management services group, a conglomerate and a century‑old beverage maker, all kept their dividend payouts unchanged, but only LHN’s dividend is backed by both profit growth and positive cash flow.

title: Singtel reports FY2026 revenue of S$14.3 bn and raises dividend 9% to S$0.185 per share
body: Singtel posted FY2026 group revenue of S$14.3 billion and underlying net profit of S$2.8 billion, driving a 9% rise in its total ordinary dividend to S$0,185 per share (core S$0,134 plus VRD S$0,051). The enterprise segment contributed over half of Singtel Singapore’s revenue, while its Australian subsidiary Optus recorded a 23% jump in FY2026 operating profit to A$550 million. Management highlighted the completion of the STT GDC transaction and the expansion of Nxera data‑centre capacity to 2.8 GW as key growth drivers, and reaffirmed a core dividend payout target of 70‑90% of underlying net profit. With a cash cushion of S$3.7 billion and a planned S$1 billion capex for the next fiscal year, Singtel aims to scale its digital infrastructure and AI services under the Singtel28 strategy.

title: Frasers Property Ltd shares rise up to 4.7% as it sells S$1.1 billion hospitality portfolio to Sirivadhanabhakdi family investment firm
body: Frasers Property Ltd announced the sale of its 63% stake in five hospitality properties in Singapore and Japan to an investment firm owned by the five children of Thai billionaire Charoen Sirivadhanabhakdi for S$1.1 billion (US$848 million). The transaction is part of a broader S$2.1 billion portfolio optimisation following the privatisation of Frasers Hospitality Trust and will lighten Frasers’ balance sheet. The deal, which requires minority shareholder approval and is slated for completion by end‑September, also includes a planned carve‑out of S$300 million of assets to be sold opportunistically within two years. After the announcement, Frasers Property’s shares rose as much as 4.7% before paring gains.

title: IREIT Global to receive €2.87 million termination fee as Allianz ends lease early
body: IREIT Global announced that its fourth‑largest tenant Allianz will terminate its lease at Concor Park early, moving the end date from May 31 2029 to Dec 31 2027. Under the early‑termination agreement Allianz will continue paying rent and service charges through Dec 31 2027 and will make a lump‑sum termination payment of about €2.87 million, roughly 5.7 % of IREIT Global’s FY2025 gross revenue. The lease previously contributed about 3.9 % of the REIT’s total gross revenue, and the manager expects no material adverse impact on distribution per unit for FY2026. IREIT Global’s units closed flat at 21 cents on June 25.

title: CGS International names DBS Group as top Singapore bank pick in its 10‑company alpha list for 2H2026
body: CGS International’s 2H2026 alpha list features six large‑cap picks—DBS Group, AEM Holdings, DFI Retail, Sembcorp Industries, iFAST Corp and SATS—each positioned for earnings resilience amid higher inflation, AI infrastructure spending and defensive growth themes. DBS Group is highlighted as the top Singapore‑bank pick with a projected FY27F dividend yield of 5.2% and strong ROE, while AEM Holdings is expected to deliver a three‑year EPS compound annual growth rate of roughly 100% driven by higher semiconductor demand. The small‑mid‑cap segment includes CSE Global (backed by a US$1.5 billion Amazon electrification contract), Marco Polo Marine (targeting about 30% FY26F revenue growth and a S$198 million new‑build order), Info‑Tech (leveraging its HRMS platform expansion), and Pan‑United (benefiting from floating‑rate construction demand). SATS aims for an 18% earnings CAGR through FY26F‑27F, iFAST Corp expects profitability improvement from stabilising staff costs and new ORSO pension scheme contributions, and Sembcorp Industries gains upside from rising spark spreads and its recent acquisition of Alinta Energy.

title: 2026 Singapore IPOs present varied growth and income opportunities
body: TOKU Ltd listed on SGX in January 2026 at S$0.25 per share, reporting FY2025 revenue of US$34.8 million (up 9.3%) and a net loss of US$9.1 million, which narrows to an adjusted loss of US$4.2 million after excluding US$4.9 million of non‑cash IPO costs. JustCo debuted in May 2026 at S$0.94 per share, operating 54 flexible‑workspace centres in 12 cities, posted FY2025 profit of US$2.7 million on US$144.2 million revenue and aims to expand to over 100 centres by 2029 with backing from GIC and Frasers Property Ltd. UIB REIT launched in March 2026 at S$0.88 per unit, holds a S$1.9 billion portfolio of 23 industrial and logistics assets, projects a FY2027 distribution yield of 7.8% and saw occupancy rise from 89.4% at IPO to 92.2% by April 2026, supported by sponsors Unified Industrial and Boustead Singapore. Investors are urged to assess each newcomer’s business fundamentals, growth prospects and valuation rather than rely on IPO hype.

title: Yangzijiang Maritime Development conducts open‑market share buyback of 426,300 shares at 58.5 cents
body: Yangzijiang Maritime Development, a maritime asset manager, purchased 426,300 shares from the open market at 58.5 cents per share. This follows an earlier open‑market repurchase on June 25 of 1 million shares at an average price of 59.25 cents. At its recent AGM, shareholders renewed a mandate allowing the company to buy back up to 348,908,852 shares, equal to 10 % of its issued share capital. The stock closed flat at 59 cents on June 26.

title: XMH Holdings proposes 11‑cent dividend as FY2026 profit rises 24.9%
body: XMH Holdings reported FY2026 profit after tax of $31.9 million, a 24.9% year‑on‑year increase, with earnings per share rising to 28.79 cents on revenue of $185.3 million. The company attributed the gain to a 27% revenue rise in its distribution segment to $109 million, while the project segment fell 7.7% to $60.5 million and after‑sales remained steady at $15.6 million. XMH proposed a total dividend of 11 cents per share—3 cents interim, 0.25 cents special and 7.75 cents final—subject to shareholder approval, and announced a 1‑for‑4 share split aimed at improving liquidity. At a closing price of $2.30, the company’s market capitalisation exceeded $264 million and the broader index is up nearly 48% year‑to‑date.

title: Weekly market roundup highlights listings and transactions at Foundation Healthcare, First REIT, StarHub, OUE REIT and Frasers Property
body: Foundation Healthcare Holdings lodged a preliminary prospectus for a Singapore Exchange mainboard listing, securing S$118.2 million from ten cornerstone investors and targeting up to S$500 million to fund clinic acquisitions and regional expansion. First REIT announced the sale of its entire Indonesia portfolio for about S$471.5 million, cutting leverage from 42.1% to 16.7% and proposing a S$9.7 million special distribution to unitholders. StarHub disclosed that Deputy CEO Matthew Williams will become CEO on 1 January 2027, succeeding Nikhil Eapen. OUE REIT will sell the Crowne Plaza Changi Airport hotel for S$500 million through OUE Hospitality Sub‑Trust, planning S$20 million of special distributions and reducing leverage to 36.6%, while Frasers Property will divest a 63% stake in five hospitality assets for S$1.1 billion, lifting pro‑forma FY2025 EPS by 3.4% and trimming net gearing by 3.3 percentage points.

title: Metech International Limited to raise about $4 million by issuing 100 million new shares at 4 cents each
body: Metech International Limited (SGX:V3M) announced a placement of 100 million new shares at 4 cents per share. The shares are being subscribed equally by Ma Ong Kee and Raffles Capital, each taking 50 million shares and ending with a 13.75% stake in Metech. The placement price represents a 2.56% premium to the volume‑weighted average price of 3.9 cents on June 26, and after estimated placement expenses the company expects net proceeds of roughly $3.98 million. The proceeds will be used for general working‑capital purposes, and Metech’s shares closed at 3.3 cents on June 26, 1.1 cents lower than the previous close.

title: Singapore Airlines shares rise 5.8% to $7.65 as Iran peace talks and World Cup boost demand
body: Singapore Airlines (SIA) shares climbed 5.8% over the week, closing at $7.65 on June 26, up from $6.27 before the May 14 earnings release. The rally was supported by the June 22 US‑Iran peace talks in Switzerland, which pushed crude oil prices lower and raised expectations of reduced jet‑fuel costs and the reopening of Middle‑East airspace. SIA also disclosed a five‑year low‑cost financing package of about 1.5 billion yuan (S$285.5 million) to fund aircraft purchases and refinance existing borrowings. Management cautioned that renewed Gulf tensions could revive fuel‑price volatility, which would weigh on costs and earnings in the 2026/2027 financial year.

title: Seatrium, Keppel and Singapore Airlines highlighted in July 2026 earnings watchlist
body: Seatrium Limited posted FY2025 revenue of S$11.5 bn, profit attributable to owners of S$323.6 m (up >100%), proposed a final dividend of S$0.03 per share and generated positive free cash flow of S$19.7 m. Keppel Ltd reported asset‑management fees of S$108 m in 1Q2026, added S$0.4 bn of new funds under management and is targeting S$2‑3 bn of non‑core asset sales in 2026, with S$385 m announced to date. Singapore Airlines Ltd recorded FY2025/2026 revenue of S$20.5 bn (up 5%), operating profit of S$2.4 bn, but net profit fell 57.4% to S$1.2 bn after the absence of a S$1.1 bn Vistara disposal gain and an S$828.5 m loss from Air India, and it declared a dividend of S$0.37 per share. Investors should watch whether Seatrium’s cash flow can sustain the doubled dividend, if Keppel’s recurring income and asset‑sale programme firm up the asset‑light pivot, and how fuel‑price pressure and Air India losses will affect Singapore Airlines’ profitability in the next reporting period.

title: Food Empire leads SGX SMID‑cap buyback wave, UOB Kay Hian sees positive signal
body: UOB Kay Hian’s June report notes that seven SGX SMID‑cap companies executed open‑market repurchases totalling about S$5.6 million, with an additional US$1.05 million bought back by UltraGreen.ai on its US‑dollar counter. Food Empire (FEH) led the activity, buying back 0.93 million shares for S$2.2 million at an average price of S$2.39, while Valuetronics (VALUE) repurchased 1.17 million shares for S$1.28 million within a S$1,078‑1,107 range and Pan‑United (PAN) bought 0.28 million shares for S$0.42 million as the stock fell from S$1.51 to S$1.44. UltraGreen.ai (UGAI) spent S$0.17 million on its SG‑dollar counter (UGS) and US$1.05 million on its US‑dollar counter and announced the acquisition of Ihld Med Tech, while Nanofilm, Winking Studios and Dezign Format also bought back shares amounting to S$1.38 million, S$0.08 million and S$0.07 million respectively. Large‑cap Venture Corp added S$1.5 million of repurchases at around S$17.35, reinforcing the view that SGX valuations remain attractive.

title: ComfortDelGro, Keppel REIT and NetLink NBN Trust pay dividends over 5% in June 2026
body: ComfortDelGro reported FY2025 revenue of S$5.06 billion, net profit of S$230.3 million and paid a FY2025 dividend of S$0,085 per share, yielding about 6.5% of profit and a current dividend yield of 6.5%. Keppel REIT posted a FY2025 distribution per unit of S$0,0523, translating to an annualised yield of 6%, with occupancy at 97.1% and aggregate leverage of 40.2% as of 31 March 2026. NetLink NBN Trust generated FY2026 revenue of S$413.4 million and EBITDA of S$282.9 million (≈68% margin) and increased its DPU to S$0,0542, delivering a dividend yield above 5%. The article stresses that while each stock offers yields above 5%, investors should evaluate cash‑flow sustainability and sector‑specific risks before relying on the high yields.

title: DBS Group Holdings and United Overseas Bank Hit Record Highs
body: DBS Group Holdings Ltd opened 2026 at a record high of S$67.00 on 23 June 2026, driven by a Q1 total income of S$5.95 billion, with wealth management delivering a record S$1.59 billion and non‑interest fees rising 19% to S$1.03 billion. The bank’s net interest income fell 5% YoY to about S$3.5 billion and NIM compressed to 1.89%, while customer deposits grew 12% to S$630 billion and loans expanded 6% to over S$453 billion. DBS raised its quarterly dividend to S$0.81 per share (ordinary S$0.66 plus a S$0.15 capital return), giving an annualised payout of S$3.24, and retains S$2.6 billion of share‑buyback capacity. United Overseas Bank Ltd also reached a new high of S$40.07 on 25 June 2026, but its Q1 total income slipped 6% to S$3.4 billion, with NII down 4% to S$2.3 billion, NIM at 1.82%, and net profit falling 4% to S$1.4 billion, and it did not declare a dividend for the quarter.

title: Soup Holdings issues profit warning after paying $384,000 pre‑termination fee
body: Soup Holdings, a restaurant operator, said it expects to report a net loss for the first half of FY2026 ending June 30 after incurring a one‑off pre‑termination fee of $384,000. The fee arose from abandoning a lease for a proposed outlet, which the company says will remove future lease commitments and operating obligations. For FY2025 the group recorded a net loss of $1.23 million on revenue of $37.5 million, and its shares last traded at 4.6 cents, valuing the company at $13.73 million. The outlet that was closed for two months was relocated and resumed operations at the end of May as part of the company’s outlet‑portfolio rationalisation.

title: AirTrunk Near Confidential Filing for Singapore's Largest IPO Since 2017
body: AirTrunk, the Blackstone‑backed data centre operator, is close to submitting a confidential draft registration for a real estate investment trust IPO in Singapore. The offering is expected to raise about US$1.5 billion (S$1.9 billion), which would be the largest Singapore IPO since 2017.
