The company was acquired by Blackstone and the Canada Pension Plan Investment Board for A$24 billion (S$21.3 billion) and is being advised on the IPO by Citigroup, DBS Group Holdings and Jefferies Financial Group. If completed, the deal would add to Singapore’s 2026 first‑time share‑sale total of US$912 million, following a US$1.9 billion tally in 2025.

title: NetLink NBN Trust, OCBC Ltd and Parkway Life REIT deliver dividend yields of 5.6%, 4% and 3.7% while remaining undervalued
body: NetLink NBN Trust, the owner of Singapore’s passive fibre network, posted FY2026 revenue of S$413.4 million and a distribution per unit of S$0,0542, giving a current yield of about 5.6% on its S$0.97 unit price. OCBC Ltd, one of Singapore’s three major banks, reported 1Q2026 net profit of S$1.97 billion (up 5% YoY) and a CET1 ratio of 17.0%, with FY2025 total dividend of S$0.99 per share translating to roughly a 4% yield at S$24.82. Parkway Life REIT, which owns healthcare properties in Singapore, Japan and France, saw FY2025 gross revenue rise 7.6% to S$156.3 million and its DPU increase to S$0,1529, resulting in a distribution yield of about 3.7% on a S$4.08 unit price, while maintaining aggregate leverage of 33.4% and interest coverage of 8.6 times. The article highlights that despite solid balance sheets and stable cash flows, each stock has lagged price appreciation, making them potential bargains for income‑focused investors.

title: DBS and OCBC poised for resilient loan growth through the second half of the year
body: Singapore banks are projected to maintain healthy loan growth in the second half of the year, with DBS and OCBC leading the expansion. MAS data showed total lending rose 10.5% year‑on‑year in May, while consumer borrowing increased 9.6% YoY despite higher inflation. Business lending is expected to stay robust, aided by front‑loaded trading ahead of the temporary 10% U.S. tariffs that expire on July 24. Lower funding costs and a slowdown in fixed‑deposit growth to 0.6% from 1.1% should limit margin compression, keeping net interest income flat in 2026 versus the prior year.

title: Monetary Authority of Singapore fines Dr Chua $120,000 for insider trading of Singapore Medical Group shares
body: The Monetary Authority of Singapore imposed a $120,000 civil penalty on Dr Chua Han Boon Kenneth for insider trading of Singapore Medical Group (SMG) shares. The regulator said Chua, a shareholder and doctor employed by a SMG subsidiary, bought 210,000 SMG shares on 6‑7 September 2022 at 32 cents each, spending $67,200, after receiving non‑public information about a privatisation bid. SMG had been listed on the Singapore Exchange’s Catalist board before being delisted in January 2023 following a voluntary privatisation offer that rose from 37 cents to 40 cents per share in late 2022. Chua has paid the penalty, admitted breaching section 218(2)(a) of the Securities and Futures Act, and undertaken not to serve as a director or be involved in company management for two years.

title: SP Group reports electricity tariffs to rise 17% in July‑September 2026
body: The Energy Market Authority announced that household electricity and gas tariffs will increase in the third quarter of 2026 due to higher natural gas prices from the Middle East conflict. SP Group said the post‑GST electricity tariff will be 31.91 cents per kWh, 4.64 cents higher than the previous quarter. For a typical four‑room HDB flat, the average monthly bill is now S$100.74 and is expected to climb to S$117.88 for July‑September, reflecting roughly a 17% tariff rise.

title: Wee Hur's Tuas View Dormitory Lease Renewal Expected, Lifting Share Overhang, CGS Says
body: CGS International analysts see a high likelihood that the land lease for Wee Hur's flagship Tuas View workers’ dormitory, which expires on 31 Oct 2026, will be extended for 2‑3 years. The dormitory contributes roughly S$84–93 million of recurring revenue with 93–95% occupancy, and the extension would remove an overhang on Wee Hur’s share price, currently at $0.65, supporting a target price of $0.95. The extension is viewed as probable because Tuas View’s 15,744 beds meet the Ministry of Manpower’s Dormitory Transition Scheme requirements amid a projected shortfall of up to 16,000 beds during 2026‑28 as construction demand drives the need for 27,000 additional workers. CGS also notes that Wee Hur’s broader order book, the new Pioneer Lodge dormitory, and growth in PBSA projects in Australia and Hong Kong provide diversification beyond the Tuas View asset.

title: Blue‑Chip Stocks in Singapore: United Overseas Bank, CapitaLand Integrated Commercial Trust and DFI Retail in Focus
body: United Overseas Bank Ltd posted a 72% profit drop to S$443 million in 3Q2025 but recovered to S$1.4 billion net income in 1Q2026, with loan growth of 4% YoY to S$354 billion, a core dividend of S$1.56 per share (14% YoY decline) and a net interest margin of 1.82%. CapitaLand Integrated Commercial Trust reported a 95.2% occupancy rate as of 31 Mar 2026, announced a S$3.9 billion acquisition of Paragon from Cuscaden Peak funded partly by a S$2.48 billion divestment of AST2 at a 9.9% premium, and its borrowing cost stands at 2.9%. DFI Retail Group Holdings Limited saw operating margin rise from a 1.8% low in 2023 to 4.1% at end‑2025 while turnover remained stable, and the group continues to run consumer brands such as Guardian, 7‑Eleven and IKEA. Investors are advised to monitor interest‑rate movements, loan‑book quality and financing costs as these macro factors influence earnings and dividend sustainability of Singapore’s blue‑chip banks, REITs and consumer staples.

title: Three SGX-listed REITs and insurer show mixed July 2026 earnings
body: Elite UK REIT reported net property income down 12.3% YoY to £9.1 million, but after stripping one‑offs adjusted NPI rose 4.0% and distributable income increased 9.8% YoY to £5.3 million, with WALE extending to 6.9 years and net gearing falling to 37.4%. First REIT saw its distribution per unit drop 13.8% YoY to S$0,00500, driven by currency effects, while underlying rental income grew 4.7% in Indonesia and 2.0% in Singapore and occupancy remained at 100%; it agreed to sell eight Indonesian hospitals to Siloam for about S$471.5 million and three non‑core assets to PT Lippo Karawaci for S$82.4 million, leaving gearing at 44.6% and debt cost at 3.9%. United Overseas Insurance, a subsidiary within the UOB Group, posted insurance revenue of S$24.9 million, down 8.8% YoY, with non‑underwriting income collapsing to S$0.1 million and total comprehensive income halving to S$5.1 million, while return on equity slipped to 2.8% and no dividend was declared. The article highlights that the headline declines for each company mask underlying improvements in cash generation or asset quality, and investors should watch inflation‑linked lease re‑gears, the execution of the Siloam hospital sale, and the recovery of investment income at UOI in the next reporting period.

title: DBS Group Holdings Ltd completes debut US$1 billion significant risk transfer
body: DBS Group Holdings Ltd announced it has completed its inaugural significant risk transfer (SRT) involving a US$1 billion (US$1.29 billion) diversified portfolio of corporate loans. The SRT allows DBS to securitise the credit risk of the loans while retaining ownership and servicing of the underlying assets. By freeing up capital, the bank aims to redeploy funds toward new lending, acquisitions and other growth opportunities, maintaining its regulatory capital ratios. The deal follows a trend, with Sumitomo Mitsui Banking Corp’s Asia Pacific arm having completed a US$3.2 billion synthetic risk transfer last year alongside Blackstone Inc, Stonepeak Partners and Clifford Capital.

title: Singapore Banks Show Resilient Income and Dividend Growth
body: Singapore’s three major banks—DBS Group, OCBC Bank and United Overseas Bank—have demonstrated resilient earnings despite economic turbulence. In 1Q2026 they reported total income of S$5.95 billion, S$3.83 billion and S$3.4 billion respectively, with DBS up 1% YoY and OCBC up 5% YoY. For FY2025 the banks returned cash to shareholders through dividends of S$3.06 per share (DBS), S$0.99 per share (OCBC) and S$1.56 per share (UOB), the latter including a special dividend of S$0.50. The Monetary Authority of Singapore’s stringent capital adequacy rules and diversified income streams—interest, wealth management and fees—support their ability to maintain strong capital ratios and generate stable cash flow.

title: EGP Energy Corporation Limited lodges preliminary IPO prospectus for SGX Mainboard listing
body: EGP Energy Corporation Limited has lodged a preliminary prospectus for an initial public offering on the Mainboard of the Singapore Exchange (SGX). The firm reported FY2023‑2025 revenues of $16.3 million, $37.9 million and $38.9 million respectively, with profit after tax of $4.1 million, $8.5 million and $10.3 million. Revenue from its key utility customer rose from 37.2% to 80.5% over the three years, and the company’s order book with that customer stood at about $239 million as of 31 May. Directors plan to recommend a dividend payout ratio of up to 40% of net profit after tax for FY2026 and FY2027, and former Starhill Global REIT CEO Ho Sing was appointed an independent director on 29 June.
